title: regime_overhaul: /frameworksInScope
description: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 is still in frameworksInScope, but for NBFCs RBI repealed it on 28 Nov 2025. It was replaced by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/363). Chapter IV and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II apply to NBFCs in the Middle Layer and above, and this entity's RBI registration N-13.09999 is nbfc-middle-layer. The successor has no vocab id and no instruments.json entry lists rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 in supersedes[], so instrument_superseded cannot be expressed. The profile is left unchanged and the regime change is flagged for re-review. Timing caveat: the repeal predates the catalog retrievedAt (2026-09-14), and the catalog version string already records it. It is reported because the profile was never refreshed and the repeal falls inside the 24-month window. Third-party IT and cyber arrangements outside the outsourcing directions fall under rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 paras 126-135, which is already in scope. From: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 (in scope as a binding instrument). To: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/363 (no vocab id). Effective date: 2025-11-28.

evidence.description: With the issue of these Directions, the existing Directions, instructions, and guidelines relating to outsourcing of financial services and IT services as applicable to NBFCs stand repealed

title: Repealed RBI outsourcing instrument still cited in frameworksInScope
statement: Because rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 remains listed in frameworksInScope after RBI repealed it on 28 Nov 2025 and replaced it with the Reserve Bank of India (NBFC - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/363), which has no vocab id, outsourcing and third-party IT risk obligations for this NBFC-middle-layer entity may be assessed against a superseded instrument instead of the current one, causing gaps in outsourcing risk management to go undetected and unreported to RBI

title: material-without-evidence: aws-mumbai (order-routing, pii/financial) has no documented exit plan
description: Material vendor (aws-mumbai is critical, supports order-routing and holds pii and financial data) has contract.exitPlanDocumented = false in contract AWS-EA-2025-0042. The contract, lastAssessment (2026-06-15, medium), rightToAudit = true and dataReturnAndDeletion = true are all present. The exit-plan gap is carried over from the baseline and was not remediated. Severity is the defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 GV.SC.S3 (medium), the most specific instrument for this SEBI mid-size RE. rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 paras 16 and 22(a) are cited as secondary refs only: that direction was repealed on 28 Nov 2025 and replaced by the RBI (NBFC - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, which have no vocab id yet. Without an exit plan, substitutability cannot be grounded either. Evidence lens: all three workspace files back the flag (aws.json services[0] aws-mumbai criticality critical, supportsCriticalFunction true, criticalFunctionRefs [order-routing], dataAccessed [pii, financial], materiality material, contract AWS-EA-2025-0042 exitPlanDocumented false, rightToAudit true, dataReturnAndDeletion true, lastAssessment 2026-06-15 medium; details.json criticalFunctions order-routing on mcp-gateway; applications/mcp-gateway/env/prod.json hosting.provider aws ap-south-1 with pii/financial data). Regulatory-mapping lens: all refs use in-scope instruments with correct regulator pairing; GV.SC.S3 is the nearest SEBI CSCRF control though its scope is supplier-contract security clauses rather than exit strategy specifically; rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 16 and 22(a) default to high but are cited only as secondary/historical refs because that instrument is repealed. Temporal-validity lens: nothing contradicts the flag; no aws finding or observation about the exit plan existed previously in the ledger; the 22(a) catalog guidance would raise this to high when substitutability is 'not-substitutable', but the vendor file records no substitutability value, so medium stands. Unverifiable: the claim that the gap was carried over from a baseline, since only the current vendor file was readable.

description: Same evidence as the SEBI PR.AA.S6 observation: at commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the HTTP transport enforces access control only when an operator explicitly sets MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS; the shipped default configuration (userConfig.ts httpHeaders: {}, deploy/azure NOAUTH template) leaves the computer resource that processes personal data reachable without any access-control check.

title: Tool-argument schemas place no bounds on the query surface reaching MongoDB
description: src/tools/args.ts's zEJSON() (lines 78-90, used for find/export filters and every non-vector-search aggregation stage) is `z.object({}).loose()` with no maxItems on the enclosing pipeline array and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values; DBOperationArgs.database and CollOperationArgs.collection (mongodbTool.ts:11-17) are plain z.string() with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike CommonArgs.string()'s NO_UNICODE_REGEX in the same repo (args.ts:22-23). This is an input-validation gap on the tool-call surface, not a rate-limiting mechanism, which this codebase does not implement at all for MCP tool calls.

title: MongoDB MCP tool schemas carry no personal-data classification markers
description: src/tools/mongodb/mongodbSchemas.ts:1-107 (and, by extension, every mongodb/* tool argsShape it feeds) defines filter, projection, document and pipeline fields as opaque EJSON or `.passthrough()` records with only a `.describe()` prose hint (e.g. `zAutoEmbedVectorSearchStageParams`, `VectorSearchStage`). No field, in this file or anywhere under src/tools/mongodb, carries a data-classification annotation (x-data-classification, x-dpdp-category, @pii or equivalent), although applications/mcp-gateway/README.md and applications/mcp-gateway/env/{qa,prod}.json declare the connected client-data and order stores pii + financial. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. zEJSON is defined as z.object({}).loose() in src/tools/args.ts:88-90; .passthrough() appears only in find.ts:22 and create/createIndex.ts:164, not in mongodbSchemas.ts itself.

title: find tool returns full unmasked documents from pii/financial collections
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/find.ts:108-118: FindTool.execute EJSON-serialises the entire cursor result set (`EJSON.stringify(cursorResults.documents)`) and returns it verbatim to the MCP client; the only applied limits are `config.maxBytesPerQuery` and `config.maxDocumentsPerQuery`, neither of which masks or filters fields. env/qa.json and env/prod.json both declare dataClassification [pii, financial] for this app. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: aggregate tool returns full unmasked pipeline results
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:187-192: AggregateTool.execute EJSON-serialises and returns the entire aggregation result set for an arbitrary user-supplied pipeline; pipelines containing `$out`/`$merge` (lines 134-141) write to a collection and send back no documents, so they are not an additional data-return path, but the read branch's result set still carries no masking or classification filter before being returned to the client. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: export tool writes full unmasked documents to an unencrypted local file
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:68-98: ExportTool.execute streams the full find/aggregate cursor to a local JSON file via ExportsManager.createJSONExport with no field mask and no encryption-at-rest on the export file; the file is exposed to the caller via a resource URI and, on stdio transport (isServerRunningLocally(), lines 131-133), its plain filesystem path. Cleanup relies on ExportsManager.close() deleting the session export directory and a best-effort TTL sweep (config.exportTimeoutMs, default 300000ms), not immediate purge. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: CreateDBUserTool returns a newly generated password in plain text
description: src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:84-96: when the tool auto-generates a password, the success content text is `User "${username}" created successfully with password: \`${password}\`.`, sent as the raw JSON-RPC tool result. `this.session.keychain.register(password, "password")` runs immediately before, but keychain-based redaction (loggerBase.ts) only scrubs subsequent logger output, not the direct tool-result payload that reaches the MCP client transcript. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: MCP HTTP transport has no default authentication requirement
description: src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319: setupMiddlewares() is the only request gate on the HTTP transport; it loops over `Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)` and rejects a request only if a configured header value mismatches. `httpHeaders` defaults to `{}` (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143), so with no operator configuration the loop performs zero comparisons and `next()` is always called: every JSON-RPC tool call is reachable unauthenticated over HTTP once the transport binds beyond loopback (httpHost defaults to 127.0.0.1; the repo's AWS Dockerfile sets host 0.0.0.0 and the Azure bicep binds to '::'). Consistent with this, deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json ships `authMode: NOAUTH` by default; a proper Azure-AD OIDC auth config exists only as an opt-in second template. env/prod.json lists this app's prod environment as exposure: partner with dataClassification [pii, financial]. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Core MongoDB tool arguments accept unbounded, unvalidated input that reaches the driver
description: src/tools/args.ts:78-90: `zEJSON()` (`z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON)`) accepts any key/value pair with no maxItems on enclosing arrays (AggregateArgs.pipeline, defined at src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:47-49) and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values, and is used as the schema for find/export `filter` and for every aggregation stage that is not `$vectorSearch`. src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17 defines `DBOperationArgs.database` and `CollOperationArgs.collection` as plain `z.string()` with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike `CommonArgs.string()` (args.ts:22-23), which applies `NO_UNICODE_REGEX` and is used for the Atlas tool arguments in the same repo. mcpHttpServer.ts:307 enforces express.json({limit: httpBodyLimit}) (default 100 KiB) and result-side caps (maxDocumentsPerQuery, maxBytesPerQuery) exist, but neither validates individual field length/shape, so per-field input validation is still missing. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: evidence-request: 3 in onfinance-db-model-master
description: Three evidence-request gaps in db-models-mongodb.default: (1) target db-models-mongodb.default.user: collection user holds personal data (user_email, user_phone_number, user_full_name, user_fcm_id, profile_pic_url), SPDI (user_password BinaryField, user_binance_auth_creds, user_debank_url) and client financial data (user_portfolio_holdings purchase_price/purchase_qty/portfolio_exposure, user_equity_portfolio_value, user_crypto_portfolio_value) with no retention setting, TTL index or expiry field anywhere in the repo. Requested: the company's record-retention schedule and the record-keeping obligation it relies on for this data. dpdp-rules-2025 8(3) requires personal data, associated traffic data and processing logs to be kept at least 365 days from the date of processing and then erased unless retention is required by law; no in-scope requirement states a fixed record-keeping period for client portfolio data, so the schedule itself is the requested evidence. (2) target db-models-mongodb.default.secrets: collection secrets stores broker trading-account credentials as plain StringField (zerodha_username, zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa, apiSecrets, accessToken) plus accountName, with no hashing, field-level encryption or TTL in the model - the same pattern as user.user_binance_auth_creds. Requested: evidence of encryption at rest or field-level encryption for these SPDI fields under dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(a), the access-control regime on the collection, and a retention/erasure schedule under dpdp-rules-2025 8(3). (3) target db-models-mongodb.default.new_discussions: several collections carry personal-data identifiers with no retention setting in code - new_discussions (author_id, author_name, author_profile_pic, sub_comments.author_id/author_name, sub_comments.banned_by), entity.social_discussions (scraped social-media author identifiers discussion_author_img/name/username and discussion_url), entity.stock_tips.expert_name, communities.community_admin_name, feedback.feedback_uid, reward.winning_user and user.users_banned. Requested: the retention/erasure schedule for these identifiers under dpdp-rules-2025 8(3), and whether the company relies on the DPDP publicly-available-data exemption for the scraped social-media author data. These are requests for evidence, not confirmed gaps. Regulatory basis: dpdp-rules-2025 8(3), 6(1)(a); sebi-cscrf-2024 ID.AM.S5.

The shipped Dockerfiles mitigate by defaulting MDB_MCP_LOGGERS=stderr,mcp (Dockerfile:7, deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12), but the library default enables the disk logger (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:58), the ENV is overridable per deployment, and the dev environment declares logsRetentionDays 30 itself (applications/mcp-gateway/env/dev.json:15). Confirm prod keeps the disk logger off and that stderr reaches the SIEM with >=180 days (prod env declares 365). Regulatory basis: cert-in-directions-2022 Dir-iv (180-day ICT system logs within India), sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S9 (two-year user access logs for critical systems), dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(e) (retain logs and personal data for one year), iso-27001-2022 A.8.15 (cited by the gap but dropped from controlIds: no iso-27001-2022 catalog file exists in regulatory-catalogs, so no control record can be created for it).

title: residency-conflict: mcp-gateway.mongodb-mcp-server.telemetry in mongodb-mcp-server
description: Target mcp-gateway.mongodb-mcp-server.telemetry: Telemetry is enabled by default (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:115; neither Dockerfile sets MDB_MCP_TELEMETRY=disabled or DO_NOT_TRACK) and the in-process worker batches events every 30 seconds (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:84) to MongoDB Inc's cloud control plane - apiBaseUrl defaults to cloud.mongodb.com (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:23), endpoints api/private/v1.0/telemetry/events and api/private/unauth/telemetry/events (src/common/atlas/apiClient.ts:200,225) - which sits outside the company's dataResidency ["IN"] and every environment's residency ["IN"]. Payloads carry device_id (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:187), session_id (src/transports/base.ts:340) and tool events incl. cluster_name (src/telemetry/types.ts:31); mongodb-redact strips keychain secrets but not device_id or session_id (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:347). A device id is pii under Maxwell's classification, making this a personal-data egress outside India under dpdp-rules-2025 Rule 15; confirm whether prod sets MDB_MCP_TELEMETRY=disabled or a processor agreement covers the flow. Regulatory basis: dpdp-rules-2025 15 (cross-border transfers subject to Central Government requirements), sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S2 (data classification and data localisation), dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(a) (unprotected personal data in the egress), dpdp-act-2023 16 and iso-27001-2022 A.5.14 (cited by the gap but dropped from controlIds: neither instrument has a catalog file in regulatory-catalogs, so no control record can be created for them).

title: schema-gap: company.metastore.pipeline in mongodb-mcp-server
description: Target company.metastore.pipeline: metastore.schema.json cannot express host-local ephemeral data-at-rest sinks: the export tool writes plaintext EJSON copies of find/aggregate results (pii and financial in prod) to the host exports folder ~/.mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports/<sessionId>/ (src/common/config/configUtils.ts:54) with a 5-minute expiry (exportTimeoutMs default 300000, src/common/config/userConfig.ts:196; files removed on shutdown, src/common/exportsManager.ts:117), and the disk logger's 30-day retention also has no home; a local folder has no credentials key to serve as endpointRef and the pipeline object has no notes or sink field, so these facts were embedded in pipeline names and gap details. Propose an optional notes (or sink location/retention) field on $defs/pipeline so runtime-probe-datapipeline gets the exports path and expiry without parsing names. Regulatory basis: sebi-cscrf-2024 ID.AM.S5 (inventories of data and metadata for designated data types).

the deploy root is registered for qa and prod (iac[].path deploy, pii/financial) and high equals the verified catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17; only quibble: qa.json exposure is internal, not partner, a wording fix to the description, not a refutation.); title: Baseline deployment parameters ship the gateway with no auth and write mode enabled
description: deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json:12 sets MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY false (overriding the template read-only default) and :21 sets authMode NOAUTH, so the shipped baseline parameters deploy an externally exposed Container App that accepts unauthenticated, write-capable MCP calls against the pii/financial client-data and order stores; the connection string entry (line 20) is a placeholder, so no secret is exposed here. The file lives in the deploy/ root registered for qa and prod and the README presents it as the baseline copy source. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every claim verified in files I opened: params_template.json lines 12 (MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY false), 20 (placeholder, no secret) and 21 (authMode NOAUTH) match the checkout, main.bicep confirms NOAUTH leaves the external ingress unauthenticated (lines 53, 135-140, 185, 153) and the read-only default (line 40) is overridden, the SARIF export contains the matching result at params_template.json:10-21 with the identical fingerprint, no overlays or compensating controls exist in the repo, deploy/ is registered as IaC for qa and prod (pii/financial, prod partner-exposed), and the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.AA.S17 is high exactly as the candidate derives; only the evidence sha256 digest could not be independently recomputed (it matches the run context sarifSha256 and the export was opened directly).); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every check passed on files I opened: sebi-cscrf-2024 applies to example-co (stock-broker/depository-participant entityTypes, active mid-size-re registration, IN jurisdiction, effective 2025-08-31, in frameworksInScope, not repealed/superseded) and is correctly the first, most specific Indian instrument; PR.AA.S17 exists in the SEBI catalog with prose squarely covering an internet-exposed API endpoint with authentication disabled (defaultSeverity high, probe-iac listed in its probeWorkflows, mid-size-re within its reCategories), PR.AA.S2 exists and its internet-exposed-infrastructure/whitelist prose relates to the exposure aspect, dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(b) exists in the DPDP catalog with access-control prose covering the gap, and ISO A.5.15 is not invented but the catalog-listed iso-27001-2022 crosswalk of dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(b), ordered last as a global mapping; severity high is correctly derived per maxwell-conventions section 4 rule 2 (no CVSS/CVE score, so the defaultSeverity of the most specific control cited, PR.AA.S17 = high, matching the SARIF rule's error level) and the cited file lines (MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY false at line 12, placeholder connection string at line 20, authMode NOAUTH at line 21) and the SARIF result with the matching fingerprint both exist; the only nuance is that DPDP Rule 6 commences 2027-05-13 per the registry structure note, but the instrument is in frameworksInScope with no draft/repealed status, the ledger convention (including dpdp-rules-2025:1 tracking phased commencement and the same run's other records citing Rule 6 clauses) cites it now, and the mapping stands independently on SEBI CSCRF, so the mapping is sound and repairable at worst by dropping the secondary DPDP ref.).

title: qa/prod deployment template defines no logging, diagnostics or SIEM forwarding
description: deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:143-182 (containerApp) and :75-84 (managedEnvironments) carry no diagnosticSettings, no Log Analytics workspace and no log forwarding of any kind; the only log configuration is the app environment variables at :38-46 writing to ephemeral container disk (/tmp/mongodb-mcp) and stderr, so platform audit and access logs are not captured, nothing reaches the Wazuh SIEM declared for prod, and the CERT-In 180-day in-India retention duty (Dir-iv) cannot be met from this deployment. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S8. SLA topics: patch-sla, log-retention. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every cited fact checks out in files I opened myself: main.bicep:143-182 (containerApp) and :75-84 (both managedEnvironments declarations, including properties:{} on the created environment) define no diagnosticSettings, Log Analytics workspace or log forwarding, a full-checkout grep finds no Microsoft.Insights/logAnalytics/operationalInsights/wazuh/fluentbit anywhere in the repo, the only log configuration is the app env vars at :38-46 (MDB_MCP_LOGGERS 'disk,mcp,stderr' to /tmp/mongodb-mcp), neither params overlay adds logging, env/qa.json and env/prod.json both register the deploy root as IaC for this repo while dev.json registers only the Dockerfile (so the 'qa/prod' title is precise) and prod.json declares the Wazuh SIEM with 365-day in-India retention, the SARIF export exists, parses and carries the bicep-no-log-diagnostics result at main.bicep:143-182 with the identical fingerprint d8a66dd2... whose sha256 matches the caller-recorded digest, the cited controls all exist (PR.AA.S8 and Dir-iv catalog texts cover exactly this gap, and 97(xi) applies since details.json shows an active nbfc-middle-layer RBI registration with rbi-outsourcing-risk-directions-2025 in scope), and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S8 as the candidate states; the ledger's prior probe-iac observation obs_01M2FVWKGWXGG3DKR0BKBP9K5S independently records the same gap and the PR.AA.S8 control record is unknown/not-tested, so there is no compensating control.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All four cited instruments apply to example-co (SEBI mid-size-re broker/DP, RBI nbfc-middle-layer, CERT-In, ISO in frameworksInScope), the controlIds PR.AA.S8, Dir-iv and 97(xi) exist in their catalogs with prose that covers the verified no-logging/no-SIEM-forwarding gap in main.bicep, SEBI CSCRF is cited first with the ISO A.8.15 crosswalk taken from the catalog mappings, and severity high correctly equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S8 since no CVSS or security-severity score exists in the candidate or the SARIF export; note only that evidence[2] duplicates evidence[0] without a description and no Azure/Microsoft vendor record exists for the CSP whose logs 97(xi) governs, neither of which is a mapping failure.).

title: Deployment location not constrained to India for an IN-residency pii/financial workload
description: deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:1-2 declares param location = resourceGroup().location with no @allowed list of Indian regions, and neither shipped parameters file sets location; the deployment guides walk through eastus (deploy/azure/README.md:53,62,71) and us-east-1 (deploy/aws/README.md:19). Environments qa and prod and the company profile declare residency IN, so this IaC permits deploying a workload that processes pii and financial order data outside India (Azure centralindia/southindia/westindia are not enforced); the actual region is only known at apply time, hence confidence possible. Note the platform mismatch recorded in the PR.IP.S13 observation (env records declare AWS EKS ap-south-1 while this root deploys Azure Container Apps). Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S13. SLA topics: patch-sla, data-localisation. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passes on files I opened: deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:1-2 declares param location = resourceGroup().location with no @allowed list, both shipped parameters files (params_template.json, paramsWithAuthEnabled_template.json) omit location, the guides walk through eastus (deploy/azure/README.md:53,62, consumed at :71) and us-east-1 (deploy/aws/README.md:19), no compensating pin, Azure Policy or CI override exists anywhere in the repo, qa and prod env records register this repo's deploy/ root as IaC with residency IN and pii/financial classification, details.json declares dataResidency IN, the prior PR.IP.S13 observation the description cites exists in the ledger, and the SARIF export exists and contains the bicep-location-no-residency-pin result at the cited lines with the identical fingerprint and severity high = the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S13; the only repairable defect is the rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:134 citation, whose control-level applicability.entityTypes (banks, SFBs, PBs, AIFIs, CICs) excludes NBFC and whose catalog guidance says the obligation is 'not carried into the NBFC Directions' while example-co is a SEBI broker with only an nbfc-middle-layer RBI arm, so the corrected refs drop it and keep SEBI first with ISO A.5.23; the SARIF sha256 digest is unverifiable (not recorded elsewhere in the workspace and not computable here) but the export was opened directly and its contents confirm the claim.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (SEBI CSCRF applies (stock-broker/depository-participant, active mid-size-re, IN) and PR.IP.S13 — cited first — exists in the SEBI catalog and its prose (cloud data in India, MeitY-empanelled CSPs, assurance that the chosen region's data centres comply; probe-iac listed) squarely covers an unpinned cloud deployment region for a pii/financial IN-residency workload, severity high correctly equals PR.IP.S13's catalog defaultSeverity (no CVSS/security-severity score in the SARIF, so maxwell-conventions section 4 step 2 applies), and ISO A.5.23 is the catalog control's own mappings[] crosswalk cited last; the one defect is the secondary ref rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:134, whose catalog entry narrows applicability.entityTypes to banks/AIFIs/CICs and states the data-location obligation is "Not carried into the NBFC Directions" while the company's only RBI entity type is nbfc — repairable by dropping that ref and its controlId, so per the lens rule (applicable clause exists, mapping repairable) the candidate is not refuted.).

title: Single replica with autoscaling disabled for the order-routing critical function
description: deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:175-179 pins minReplicas=1 and maxReplicas=1 with an empty rules array whose comment explicitly disables autoscaling, and the template defines no DR site or second region. mcp-gateway carries the order-routing critical function (details.json impact tolerance 30 minutes outage; SEBI RTO expectation 2 hours), so a single instance leaves no spare capacity for a node or zone failure or a load spike in qa/prod, and the gateway serving the client-data and order stores goes down with it. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:RC.RP.S1. SLA topics: patch-sla, backup-rto-rpo. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every claim verifies against files I opened: main.bicep:175-179 pins minReplicas=1/maxReplicas=1 with 'rules: [] // disables autoscaling' and (whole file read) defines no DR site or second region; it is the only .bicep in the repo with neither params_template.json, paramsWithAuthEnabled_template.json nor any script overriding the hardcoded scale block, and env qa.json/prod.json register the deploy root for mongodb-mcp-server; details.json confirms the order-routing critical function with appIds mcp-gateway and maxOutageMinutes 30; the SARIF export exists, parses, and contains the bicep-single-replica-no-ha result at deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:175-179 with the identical fingerprint, severity high equal to the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:RC.RP.S1 (RBI 171 also exists and applies to nbfc-middle-layer), and the ledger holds no implemented control for RC.RP.S1 (unknown/not-tested) and no prior use of the fingerprint; the only defect is a redundant duplicate of the sarif evidence entry.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All regulatory-mapping checks pass: sebi-cscrf-2024 applies (entityTypes stock-broker/depository-participant, active mid-size-re SEBI registrations, IN, in frameworksInScope) and is cited first with RC.RP.S1, which exists in the SEBI catalog with defaultSeverity high and prose covering spare capacity, cloud high-availability and cross-region recovery with probe-iac among its probeWorkflows, matching the single-replica/no-DR gap in the SARIF result; rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 applies via the active nbfc-middle-layer registration and control 171 exists in its catalog with nbfc-middle-layer in reCategories and covers minimal RTO/near-zero RPO for critical information systems; the ISO A.5.30 ref is a genuine catalog crosswalk (listed in RBI 171's mappings, and of SEBI RC.RP.S2), not invented; severity high is correctly derived from RC.RP.S1's catalog defaultSeverity because the exported SARIF rule carries no security-severity or CVSS score, and details.json confirms the order-routing critical function with maxOutageMinutes 30 on appIds mcp-gateway as the description claims.).

title: Dev-root Dockerfile installs the server and base image unpinned (latest by default)
description: Dockerfile:1 uses FROM node:24-alpine (mutable tag, no digest), :2 declares ARG VERSION=latest and :4 runs npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server using that build arg, so a default build of the dev environment IaC root (env/dev.json iac[].path Dockerfile) resolves whatever the public npm registry and Docker Hub serve at build time, with no integrity verification. The release workflow passes VERSION explicitly (.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml), but local and dev builds default to latest. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every cited evidence file exists and shows the claim: the SARIF export contains result dockerfile-unpinned-package-install at Dockerfile:1-4 with the identical fingerprint adbb10d5ee6d6449e96dc20233569e5a0f2f9e9e0b06ce71475f0143f3adbe8c, the checkout Dockerfile exhibits the gap (line 1 FROM node:24-alpine with no digest, line 2 ARG VERSION=latest, line 4 RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@${VERSION}), env/dev.json registers this exact path as the dev IaC root, the only pinning in the repo is .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml passing VERSION explicitly for release builds — which the description itself acknowledges while local/dev builds default to latest, and no compose/Makefile/overlay override exists — and severity high equals both the SARIF rule's defaultSeverity and the catalog PR.DS.S6 defaultSeverity (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3551); note for the regulatory-mapping pass only: PR.DS.S6's applicability lists mii/qualified-re while example-co's SEBI registrations are category mid-size-re, which is outside this evidence lens; evidence[2] is a redundant duplicate of evidence[0] but resolves to the same valid export, so it does not refute.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Both cited instruments apply to example-co (sebi-cscrf-2024 binds an active mid-size-re stock broker/DP and is correctly first; iso-27001-2022 is in frameworksInScope) and severity high is a correct catalog-defaultSeverity derivation with no CVSS basis in the SARIF, but the mapping is defective and repaired rather than refuted: control PR.DS.S6 does not bind this company (applicability.reCategories is mii+qualified-re only and its prose says 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26)' while details.json records both SEBI registrations as active mid-size-re), and the ISO crosswalk A.5.21 is invented (PR.DS.S6's catalog mappings list ISO A.5.20 and A.8.30, and A.5.21's cloud-services governance text does not cover build-time software pinning), so the primary ref is corrected to the all-RE mandatory control sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5 (SBOM with cryptographic hashes of components for core and critical software, in-house and third-party alike — covering the unpinned mongodb-mcp-server@latest / node:24-alpine install behind the order-routing-critical mcp-gateway; defaultSeverity high so severity stays high) with GV.SC.S5's own catalog crosswalk NIST SSDF PS.3.2 as the global secondary.).

title: AWS deploy-root Dockerfile hardcodes @latest npm install for the qa/prod image
description: deploy/aws/Dockerfile:9 hardcodes RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest, ignoring ARG VERSION declared at :3, and :2 builds FROM node:24-alpine without a digest: the Bedrock AgentCore image built from the deploy/ root registered for qa and prod contains whatever the public npm registry and Docker Hub served at build time, with no version, digest or checksum verification for a regulated workload. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every check passed: the checkout's deploy/aws/Dockerfile shows exactly the claimed gap (line 2 FROM node:24-alpine with no digest, line 3 ARG VERSION=latest, line 9 hardcoded RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest ignoring the ARG), the SARIF export at the cited path contains the matching fail result for ruleId dockerfile-unpinned-package-install at deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2-9 with the identical fingerprint d5bf6aa5...493179 and pinned commit aaa72a04..., env/qa.json and env/prod.json both register this repo's deploy root under iac[] so the build recipe is reachable for the pii/financial qa and prod workloads, no compensating control exists (docker-publish.yml pins VERSION only for the root Dockerfile with context '.', no workflow builds deploy/aws/Dockerfile, deploy/aws/README.md itself pushes an unpinned :latest to ECR, and the hardcoded @latest could not be pinned by a build arg anyway), and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 which covers software integrity verification; note evidence[2] is a bare duplicate of evidence[0] with no description, which is redundant but harmless under this lens.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Repairable mis-mapping, not a refutation: the primary and severity-determining control sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 is inapplicable to example-co — its catalog entry narrows applicability.reCategories to [mii, qualified-re] and its prose says 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26)' while both of example-co's active SEBI registrations are mid-size-re — and the secondary ref iso-27001-2022:A.5.21 (the cloud-services control, used in this workspace's catalogs only for vendor/cloud third-party arrangements such as RBI 2026 para 126 and absent from every applicable control's mappings[]) does not cover the unpinned npm install and undigested base image; the gap (no version, digest or checksum verification for the order-routing critical function's image, from the deploy root registered in env/qa.json and env/prod.json) is covered by sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5, which requires an SBOM with cryptographic hashes of components for all core and critical software in-house and third-party alike, has no category narrowing, and carries defaultSeverity high so severity 'high' stands (no CVSS score exists in the candidate or the SARIF export), and the iac-auditor's generic IAC-DRIFT-01 checklist row (which prescribes PR.DS.S6 regardless of RE category and whose own global crosswalks are nist-ssdf-800-218:PW.4.1 and cis-controls-8.1:16.11, not ISO A.5.21) cannot override the catalog's control-level applicability; outside this lens, evidence[2] byte-duplicates evidence[0].).

MCP HTTP transport endpoint ships without authentication or rate limiting
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the gateway's HTTP transport exposes POST/GET/DELETE /mcp with no authentication by default: the only mechanism is exact-match validation of the operator-configured httpHeaders map which defaults to an empty object (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143), there is no rate limiter, no 429/409 handling, no TLS in the express app, and with externallyManagedSessions=true a client-supplied mcp-session-id creates a session without authentication (src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-419). The optional monitoring server exposes /health and /metrics unauthenticated (src/transports/monitoring.ts:53-79). Deployed to prod (eks-prod-mumbai, exposure partner, pii+financial), any in-cluster caller can call every enabled tool against the client-data and order stores. No gateway policy exists in the repo.

title: Tool-argument validation is strong for Atlas identifiers but open for database-bound payloads
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0, Atlas arguments are well constrained (24-char hex objectIds, cluster-name and username regexes, ipv4/cidrv4, enums: src/tools/args.ts:22-76), but every MongoDB-bound payload flows through zEJSON() = z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) (src/tools/args.ts:86-90) with no key, length, pattern or maxItems constraint; database and collection names are unbounded z.string() (src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17) and the stdio payload limit is advertised as informational only (src/transports/constants.ts:15-17). See finding SCH-API-02.

title: Credentials traverse the tool surface in plaintext while config-supplied secrets are redacted
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the connect, switch-connection and atlas-create-db-user tools accept live credentials (connection strings with embedded username/password, DB-user passwords) as plain z.string() tool arguments, and atlas-create-db-user echoes a generated password back in the tool response (src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:93). Compensating controls exist: every config-supplied secret is registered in the root keychain for redaction (src/common/config/parseUserConfig.ts:157-180), disk logs and telemetry redact keychain secrets by default, and tool error responses are redacted against keychain.allSecrets (src/tools/tool.ts:818-829). See findings SCH-API-06.

title: Credential issuance via tools is partially controlled; destructive-tool approval fails open
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0, temporary Atlas DB users are created with CSPRNG passwords and a deleteAfterDate expiry (src/tools/atlas/connect/connectCluster.ts:104-131) and the config resource masks credentials (src/resources/common/config.ts:34-50), which are positive practices. However credentials are also accepted and echoed through tool arguments (findings SCH-API-06 on connect.ts, switchConnection.ts, createDBUser.ts) and the human-approval gate for destructive tools fails open for clients without elicitation support (src/elicitation.ts:30-33), defeating least-privilege execution for headless agent clients; the company aiCodingPolicy requires human-approval-for-writes.

evidence.description: SCH-API-06 results, mcp-tool-confirmation-fails-open result, mcp-config-resource-masks-credentials pass result

title: export tool writes client data to plaintext EJSON files on the host filesystem
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the export tool streams find/aggregate results (pii+financial per env/prod.json) into plaintext JSON files with no encryption, file-mode restriction or KMS reference (src/common/exportsManager.ts:198-249, default folder ~/.mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports). Retention is short (5-minute expiry, cleanup interval, recursive delete on shutdown) which partially compensates, but during their life files are unencrypted and are also exposed by raw filesystem path (src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:119-124). See finding SCH-PII-02. SLA topic: encryption.

title: Gateway tool-call logs kept 30 days with no user identification
description: mcp-gateway is in the appIds of the order-routing critical function (company-profile/example-co/details.json), so its access logs are CSCRF critical-system user logs. At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the on-disk application log is created with retentionDays 30 and gzip false (src/common/logging/diskLogger.ts:21-29), the default loggers are disk and mcp (stderr excluded, src/common/config/userConfig.ts:47-63), and log lines carry a sessionId attribute only with no end-user identity (src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:263). 30 days is below the CSCRF two-year requirement for critical-system user logs.

title: Log hygiene is partly implemented: secret redaction present, stdout shipping absent by default
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 tool error responses and disk/telemetry output are redacted against session keychain secrets (src/tools/tool.ts:813-829, src/common/logging/loggerBase.ts:42-67, src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:339-352), satisfying secure handling. However the default logger set [disk,mcp] excludes stderr, so application logs are not on the container-native collection path unless operators change config, and the disk store keeps only 30 days (see PR.AA.S9 observation).

title: Exports have a working disposal lifecycle; component logs do not meet the retention schedule
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 the export artefact has a real disposal mechanism: expiry after exportTimeoutMs (default 300000 ms, request overrides only lower it), a cleanup interval (src/common/exportsManager.ts:297-338) and recursive deletion on shutdown (lines 110-126) - satisfied for that artefact class. The gateway's own log store retains 30 days hardcoded (src/common/logging/diskLogger.ts:23) which does not reconcile with the env platform retention (365 days) unless the disk store is shipped to the SIEM, and no retention annotation exists for data that leaves via telemetry.

title: Tool schemas carry no classification tags and default-on telemetry sends usage metadata to cloud.mongodb.com
description: Per the catalog guidance the localisation limb of PR.DS.S2 is in abeyance under CIR/2024/184, so localisation gaps are recorded as observations, not findings. At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 no classification annotation exists anywhere in the zod tool schemas, and telemetry defaults to enabled (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:113-117), sending device_id (machine id, src/helpers/deviceId.ts:20-24), session_id, tool names and cluster metadata to https://cloud.mongodb.com/ every 30 seconds (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:184-190, 390-398, apiBaseUrl default line 21-24); assistant search queries go to https://knowledge.mongodb.com/api/v1/ (assistantBaseUrl default, line 25-29). This is IT and Cybersecurity-Data-style usage metadata rather than Regulatory Data, but the annual IT-Committee review and classification register the control expects are not evidenced, and the EKS stores are all ap-south-1. Readiness secondary mapping: dpdp-rules-2025:15.

evidence.description: manual review of ServerConfigSchema and telemetry pipeline
pipeline mongodb-mcp-telemetry: device_id, session_id and tool events to the Atlas cloud telemetry API

title: Prompt-injection wrapping present on tool responses; exported data has no leak controls
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 find/aggregate/search-knowledge responses wrap untrusted document content in unique untrusted-user-data tags with instructions not to act on embedded content (src/tools/tool.ts:967-994) - a satisfied leak-prevention measure for the LLM channel. Against that, export output (full documents) lands on the host filesystem in plaintext with no DLP or masking control (finding SCH-PII-02), and find/aggregate return raw document fields to the client with no field masking or projection policy despite the metastore classifying reachable collections (secrets, user) as restricted/spdi/pii.

evidence.description: db-models-mongodb catalog: secrets and user collections classified restricted/spdi/pii

title: mcp-gateway has no catalogued data inventory despite querying the client-data and order stores
description: The metastore records three pipelines for this repo (mongodb-mcp-tool-handler, mongodb-mcp-export-tool, mongodb-mcp-telemetry) but the mcp-gateway-mongodb catalog lists zero schemas, so the datasets this gateway reads and writes are not inventoried under this app; the reachable collections are catalogued under the db-models app (secrets, user, webinar, communities, new_discussions, entity, insights*, notifications, feedback, reward, cached_chats). No classification, PII or retention annotation exists in the repo's own zod schemas either. The README states data classes pii and financial, while sdlc/policy.json aiCodingPolicy allows only public/internal data classes for AI tooling - a scope disagreement the ledger should carry as risk.

evidence.description: mcp-gateway-mongodb catalog schemas empty; db-models-mongodb catalog populated; three mcp-gateway pipelines
gateway lets AI agents query the client-data and order stores; data classes pii, financial

title: Data flows are recorded in the metastore but per-hop encryption is not mapped and one hop is plaintext
description: The metastore pipelines record the tool-handler flow (runtime-configured MongoDB cluster), the export flow (plaintext EJSON files in the host exports folder, 5-minute expiry) and the telemetry flow (device_id, session_id, tool events to the MongoDB Atlas cloud telemetry API every 30 seconds). The export hop is plaintext on the host filesystem (finding SCH-PII-02) and the crypto methods per hop are not recorded; no cryptographic inventory exists in the repo. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Gateway component logs retained 30 days on disk; platform retention is 365 days in India if shipped
description: The gateway's own application log is hardcoded to a 30-day rolling retention (src/common/logging/diskLogger.ts:21-29, gzip false, retentionGB 1), below the CERT-In 180-day mandate, and the default loggers [disk,mcp] exclude stderr so the log is not on the container stdout path. The platform observability for prod retains logs 365 days in India (env/prod.json), which satisfies the direction only if this on-disk store is shipped to the SIEM; that shipping is not visible in the checkout, so the component-level posture is partial. See finding SCH-RET-03. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

evidence.description: logsRetentionDays 365, logsInIndia true, SIEM Wazuh ap-south-1

title: mcp-gateway is a consumer, not a provider, of cloud services
description: ExampleCo only consumes cloud and VPN services; it operates no data-centre, VPS, consumer-VPN or cloud-service offering through mcp-gateway, so the subscriber-registration duty does not bind this subject (catalog guidance: record not-applicable with reasoning). No subscriber-onboarding schema exists in the checkout.

evidence.description: full schema inventory found no subscriber/customer-onboarding model

title: ExampleCo is not a virtual-asset service provider
description: The company is a SEBI stock broker, depository participant and NBFC; it operates no virtual-asset exchange, brokerage, custodian or wallet, so the five-year KYC/transaction-record duty (and the Annexure III KYC annex referenced by it) does not bind this repo. No virtual-asset ledger schema exists in the checkout.

evidence.description: entityTypes stock-broker, depository-participant, nbfc; no VASP registration

title: No CIA classification on the gateway's data surfaces (NBFC middle layer)
description: For the NBFC arm, paragraph 36 requires security classification of information assets. The zod schemas across the tool surface carry no classification annotation (no isSecret-style tagging outside config secrets, no data-classification metadata on tool arguments or outputs), and the metastore's mcp-gateway-mongodb catalog is empty. Config secrets are the exception: userConfig.ts marks apiClientId, apiClientSecret, connectionString and voyageApiKey isSecret. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

evidence.description: manual classification review of all zod schemas

title: Paragraph 48 is not carried into the NBFC Directions
description: The catalog applicability for paragraph 48 lists banks, SFBs, payments banks, AIFIs, CICs and UCBs only and notes the obligation is not carried into the NBFC Directions; ExampleCo is registered as an NBFC middle layer with no banking licence, so this control does not bind. The binding classification control for the NBFC arm is paragraph 36, recorded separately.

evidence.description: control 48 applicability excludes nbfc; guidance notes not carried into the NBFC Directions

title: Gateway data dictionary is empty in the metastore while the tool surface is self-describing
description: The metastore is Maxwell's dictionary reconciliation point; the mcp-gateway-mongodb catalog lists zero schemas although the repo registers a fully self-describing tool surface (zod argsShape and outputSchema per tool, exposed as JSON Schema to MCP clients). The reachable collections are documented only under the db-models app's catalog. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

evidence.description: mcp-gateway-mongodb schemas: [] vs populated db-models-mongodb catalog

title: No deprecated crypto in code, but exported sensitive data is unencrypted
description: At commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 no deprecated or weak algorithm is used (temporary passwords use 16-byte CSPRNG base64url, src/helpers/generatePassword.ts; no MD5/SHA-1 in the schema surface; TLS to MongoDB endpoints is driver-managed). The probe-schemas limb of paragraph 140 - sensitive fields encrypted or tokenised - is not met for export output: find/aggregate results are written to plaintext files (finding SCH-PII-02) and returned to the client without field-level masking.

title: No consent-notice surface exists in this repo (readiness mapping)
description: Rule 3 commences 2027-05-13 (instruments.json structure: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 come into force eighteen months after publication), so this is a readiness mapping, not a live obligation, and in any case mcp-gateway is a query interface over data stores owned by other applications: it hosts no onboarding, consent or notice flow. The notice obligation sits with the onboarding applications. No consent_artefact, notice_version or purpose field exists in any zod schema in the checkout.

evidence.description: full tool-surface review found no consent or notice fields

title: Umbrella safeguards partial: redaction exists, but endpoint auth, credential handling and export encryption have gaps
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 (including Rule 6) commence 2027-05-13, so this is recorded as a readiness gap at catalog severity, not a live breach. Derived from the sub-clause observations in this audit: 6(1)(a) encryption partial (plaintext exports), 6(1)(b) access control not satisfied (no endpoint authentication, approval fails open), 6(1)(e) log retention not satisfied (30-day component logs), while positive safeguards exist (keychain redaction, untrusted-data wrapping, temporary-user expiry). Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

evidence.description: all fail and pass results of this run

title: Personal data exported to plaintext files; query responses unmasked (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rule 6 commences 2027-05-13. The export pipeline writes query results containing personal data (client-data and order stores) to plaintext EJSON files with no encryption, tokenisation or masking annotation (finding SCH-PII-02 on src/common/exportsManager.ts:198-249), and find/aggregate return raw documents to the MCP client with no field-masking mechanism anywhere in the tool surface. Compensating: exports expire in 5 minutes and are deleted on shutdown.

title: Tool-call endpoint has no default access control and destructive approval fails open (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rule 6 commences 2027-05-13. The HTTP transport validates no authentication by default (httpHeaders empty object, finding SCH-API-01), tool calls are authorised only by the optional readOnly/disabledTools config (both default permissive), and the confirmation gate for destructive tools returns true for clients without elicitation support (finding mcp-tool-confirmation-fails-open). No user identity is propagated from MCP clients into sessions (session id only).

title: Component logs retained 30 days, below the one-year floor (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rule 6 commences 2027-05-13. The gateway's own application log - the only record of which tools touched which collections - is hardcoded to 30 days (src/common/logging/diskLogger.ts:21-29) and is not on the container stdout path by default, below the one-year retention this rule expects for detection and investigation of unauthorised access. The platform SIEM retains 365 days in India, which satisfies the floor only if this log store is shipped there.

title: Company does not fall in a Third Schedule class (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. Rule 8(1) binds only e-commerce entities with two crore or more registered users in India, online gaming intermediaries with fifty lakh or more, and social media intermediaries with two crore or more; a stock broker, DP and NBFC does not fall in any Third Schedule class. The broker-wide erasure duty comes from Act-8(7), recorded separately.

title: Gateway processing logs kept 30 days; export artefacts erased in minutes (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. The gateway's tool-call log covers only 30 days (finding SCH-RET-03), while export artefacts carry a real expire-and-erase lifecycle (5-minute expiry, cleanup cycle, recursive delete on shutdown) which amply meets the erasure limb for that artefact. The one-year retention limb for processing records of the underlying stores sits with the data-owner applications, not this repo.

evidence.description: SCH-RET-03 result and manual review of ExportsManager lifecycle

title: No child-data fields on this surface (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. No date-of-birth, age, guardian, guardian-consent or minor-account field exists in any zod schema in the checkout or in the tool surface; minor-account onboarding (if any) sits with the data-owner applications. Nothing in this repo processes or distinguishes child data.

description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. The gateway holds no guardianship-reference or verification-event fields in any schema; consent flows belong to the onboarding applications.

title: Internal gateway has no Data-Principal-facing rights channel (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. mcp-gateway is an internal AI-agent query interface with no Data-Principal-facing endpoint; the published means for rights requests belong to the customer-facing applications. No rights-request schema exists in the checkout.

evidence.description: full tool-surface review found no rights-request surface

title: No rights-request intake in this repo (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. Companion to 14(1): this repo exposes no intake for rights requests, so acceptance behaviour cannot be assessed here; it belongs to the customer-facing applications.

evidence.description: full tool-surface review found no rights-request surface

title: No nominee fields on this surface (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rules 3 and 5 to 16 commence 2027-05-13. No nomination facility or nominee field exists in the gateway's schemas; nomination belongs to the customer master data of the onboarding applications.

evidence.description: full tool-surface review found no nominee fields

title: Default-on telemetry and assistant egress send usage identifiers outside India (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Rule 15 commences 2027-05-13. Telemetry defaults to enabled and ships device_id (a persistent machine identifier of the operating employee), session_id and tool-usage metadata to https://cloud.mongodb.com/ every 30 seconds (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts, src/helpers/deviceId.ts:20-24), and assistant search sends raw query text to https://knowledge.mongodb.com/api/v1/ (src/tools/assistant/searchKnowledge.ts). No cross-border transfer register or restriction covers these flows in the repo; env residency is IN and all stores are ap-south-1. For the SEBI arm this is IT-and-Cybersecurity-Data-style usage metadata reviewed under the PR.DS.S2 abeyance observation.

title: Open schemas allow unvalidated writes to client stores (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Act section 8(3) commences 2027-05-13. insert-many and update-many accept entirely unconstrained documents through zEJSON() (z.object({}).loose()) so no completeness, accuracy or consistency check exists on personal data written through the gateway (finding SCH-API-02); find/aggregate output schemas exist for some tools but none validate content fields. Accuracy duties for the underlying customer master sit with the data-owner applications.

title: Erasure orchestration belongs to the data-owner applications (readiness mapping)
description: Readiness mapping: Act section 8(7) commences 2027-05-13. The gateway is an access layer over stores owned by other applications: it exposes generic delete-many/drop tools but no retention schedule, consent-withdrawal trigger or erasure job; nothing in this repo decides when personal data is erased. The only erasure lifecycle it owns (export files) is short-lived and deletes reliably.

description: The First Schedule consent-manager obligations (rule 4 and Schedule 1 commence 2026-11-13 per the registry) bind a company operating a consent platform; ExampleCo runs no consent-manager or account-aggregator platform in mcp-gateway, which exposes only MongoDB, Atlas and assistant tools. No consent-request or onboarded-fiduciary registry schema exists in the checkout.
