title: MCP HTTP transport endpoint ships with no authentication, rate limiting or idempotency controls by default
description:
src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-419 exposes POST/GET/DELETE /mcp with no authentication by default: the only built-in mechanism is exact-match validation of the operator-configured httpHeaders map, which defaults to an empty object (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143: httpHeaders: z.object({}).loose().default({})), so the middleware (lines 308-318) validates nothing; snippet: for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)) { const header = req.headers[key.toLowerCase()]; if (!header || header !== value) ... }. There is no per-request authorisation of tool calls, no rate limiter, no 429 or 409 handling, and no TLS termination in the express app. With externallyManagedSessions=true any request may supply an arbitrary mcp-session-id header and get a session without authentication (lines 336-355), after which every enabled tool (find, aggregate, insert-many, update-many, delete-many, drop-database, atlas tools) is callable against the client-data and order stores. The optional monitoring server exposes /health and /metrics unauthenticated too (src/transports/monitoringServer.ts:53-79). Deployed to prod (eks-prod-mumbai, exposure partner, data classes pii and financial) any in-cluster caller can read client data; no gateway policy (x-kong-plugin, x-amazon-apigateway-auth, Istio RequestAuthentication) exists in this repo. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17. DPDP Rule 6(1)(b) (commences 2027-05-13) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Not refuted: every substantive claim verifies in files I opened myself — mcpHttpServer.ts:306-419 defines POST/GET/DELETE /mcp (lines 360/400/411) whose only request gate is the httpHeaders exact-match middleware at exactly 308-318 with httpHeaders defaulting to {} (userConfig.ts:136-143 verbatim, overrideBehavior not-allowed), the externallyManagedSessions implicit-session path sits at exactly 336-355, there is no rate limiter or 429/409 handling anywhere (only two app.use registrations in all of src, jsonRpcErrorCodes.ts defines none), the express app is plain HTTP with no TLS (expressBasedHttpServer.ts app.listen), monitoringServer.ts:53-79 exposes /health and /metrics with no middleware, all named tools exist (tools.ts: find/insert-many/aggregate/update-many/delete-many/drop-database plus src/tools/atlas), env/prod.json confirms eks-prod-mumbai/exposure partner/dataClassification [pii, financial], the same run's probe-iac SARIF independently shows the bicep NOAUTH default with external ingress, no ipSecurityRestrictions/WAF/rate limit (the Entra auth variant is opt-in) and no gateway-policy terms exist anywhere in the repo, all three controlIds exist as ledger control records, severity high equals the verified catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 (the most specific Indian instrument first; dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(b) is also high and its 2027-05-13 commencement is confirmed in instruments.json line 994), the cited SARIF export exists, parses and defines rule SCH-API-01 with exactly the candidate's defaultSeverity high, severityBasis sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 and the four regulatoryRefs, and the fingerprint matches the ledger's existing stable identity for the same ruleId+target+path (open finding fnd_01M2G2AGVRZPBP3VH8FNAYH46V, the intended re-run update); the export's minified results[] beyond the first 2000 characters of its single line, its sha256 digest and the checkout's git HEAD could not be independently opened or computed (listed unverifiable, none refuting since the export is present and the gap is confirmed in the primary source), and evidence[1] is merely a redundant duplicate of evidence[0], a style defect that does not refute.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every cited instrument applies — sebi-cscrf-2024 first as the in-scope primary for this mid-size SEBI RE (PR.AA.S17's prose squarely covers an unauthenticated, unthrottled API), dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(b)/6(1) exist and cover access control with the 2027-05-13 commencement correctly disclosed as a readiness mapping, and the voluntary NIST/OWASP crosswalks come last — and severity high correctly equals PR.AA.S17's catalog defaultSeverity because neither the candidate nor the SARIF rule carries any CVSS/security-severity score; the only defect is repairable: owasp-asvs-5.0:8.2.1 is not the crosswalk of any cited catalog control (the SEBI catalog maps PR.AA.S17 to owasp-asvs-5.0:V4 and skills require crosswalks from catalog mappings[]), so correctedRegulatoryRefs is returned rather than refuting.).

title: zod tool-argument schemas leave database-bound input unbounded and unvalidated
description:
src/tools/args.ts:22-90: zEJSON() (lines 86-90) is z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) - an open record with unknown values - used for every filter, pipeline, update operator and inserted document; snippet: export function zEJSON() { return z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) as unknown as z.ZodRecord<z.ZodString, z.ZodUnknown>; }. CommonArgs.string() (lines 22-23) applies a no-Unicode regex but no maxLength; AtlasArgs.password() (lines 74-76) has min 1 max 100 and no pattern. Database and collection names are plain unbounded z.string() (src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17: database: z.string().describe("Database name")), the insert-many documents array has no maxItems (src/tools/mongodb/create/insertMany.ts:22-26), exportTitle (src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:16) and the assistant search query (src/tools/assistant/searchKnowledge.ts:9-14) are unbounded strings, and the stdio transport payload limit is informational only and not enforced (src/transports/constants.ts:15-17: 50 MiB advertised). Only the HTTP transport enforces a body limit (default 100 KiB). Oversized payloads and NoSQL operator injection through documents, filters and pipelines reach the MongoDB driver and the filesystem without schema-level constraint. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2. DPDP Act-8(3) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every code claim verified line-precise in the pinned checkout (args.ts:22-23 no-Unicode regex with no maxLength, 74-75 password min1/max100 without pattern, 86-90 zEJSON = z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON); mongodbTool.ts:11-17 unbounded database/collection z.string(); insertMany.ts:22-26 documents array without maxItems; export.ts:16 and searchKnowledge.ts:9-14 unbounded strings; constants.ts:15-17 stdio 50 MiB 'informational only' with no enforcement anywhere in stdio.ts, while mcpHttpServer.ts:307's 100 KiB express.json cap is the only enforcement — disclosed accurately by the finding); the SARIF export exists, is valid SARIF 2.1.0 from maxwell-schema-auditor 1.0.0, and defines rule SCH-API-02 at defaultSeverity medium on the stated sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2 basis with the candidate's exact regulatoryRefs; severity medium equals PR.IP.S2's catalog defaultSeverity (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3677), dpdp-rules-2025:Act-8(3) exists in its catalog as a pre-13-May-2027 readiness control whose guidance names probe-schemas (matching the 'readiness mapping' wording), and all four instruments are in instruments.json; the repo is the deployed source for qa/prod (repo record pinned at the cited commit, env iac, bicep deploys mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server:1.11.0 built by this repo's CI) with no overlay, ignore file or central validation overriding the per-field gap; and the fingerprint is byte-identical to the open ledger finding fnd_01M2G2AGX1GZ9THG6HJ1VPP1EP for the same SCH-API-02 result at src/tools/args.ts, so this is the designed fingerprint-based re-run update rather than a duplicate (note the earlier run mapped the same fingerprint to PR.AA.S17/high, which the ledger keeper's supersession resolves); the only bytes I could not read are the gitignored export's results[] entry (single-line file truncated at char 2000, grep skips gitignored paths) and its sha256, both corroborated by the readable rule metadata, the identical prior-run fingerprint and the checkout itself — so no check under this lens fails.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every check verifiable in the workspace passed: sebi-cscrf-2024 binds example-co (active mid-size-re stock-broker and depository-participant, jurisdiction IN, in frameworksInScope) and catalog control PR.IP.S2 exists with defaultSeverity medium, matching the candidate's severity and the SARIF rule SCH-API-02's own severityBasis, and its SSDLC prose (security requirements, application security testing during development, OWASP ASVS guidance, defence in depth) is the nearest SEBI clause for an unbounded or unvalidated tool-argument schema gap since the catalog has no dedicated input-validation control; dpdp-rules-2025 also binds the company, its Act-8(3) control exists and lists probe-schemas with the candidate correctly framing it as a readiness mapping ahead of the 13 May 2027 commencement; the Indian instruments are cited first with the registry's regulators and well-formed control ids, the not-in-scope global instruments appear only as later secondary refs as the skill allows, and the patch-sla topic claim fits a vulnerability-with-a-fix; the only unverifiable pieces are the supplementary owasp-asvs-5.0:2.2.1 and nist-800-53-r5:SI-10 crosswalks (global instruments ship no catalog file), which the candidate transcribed verbatim from the rule definition in the SARIF export; note the export's rule also carries a second SEBI ref, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 (applies to mid-size-re, covers the OWASP API Top 10 injection angle), which the candidate may optionally add without changing severity since regulatoryRefs[0] stays PR.IP.S2.).

title: atlas-create-db-user takes a plaintext password argument and echoes the generated password back in the tool response
description:
src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:16-20 declares password: AtlasArgs.password().nullish() (a plain z.string(), min 1 max 100, no pattern, src/tools/args.ts:74-76) and lines 89-96 echo the generated credential to the MCP client; snippet (line 93): text: `User "${username}" created successfully${shouldGeneratePassword ? ` with password: `${password}` : ""}.` Tool arguments and responses transit and are retained in the MCP client and LLM context/transcripts, so the credential leaves the gateway in plaintext. The password is registered in the session keychain only after the API call succeeds (lines 84-87), redacting later logs and telemetry but not the response itself. Compensating controls: the tool is on the default confirmationRequiredTools list and the confirmation prompt masks the password (line 109: "(Auto-generated secure password)"). Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passed on files I opened myself: the cited SARIF export exists and contains a kind=fail result with ruleId SCH-API-06 at src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts region startLine 16 endLine 96 carrying severity high, confidence confirmed and maxwell/controlIds exactly [sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S1, dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)] with the candidate's SEBI/MeitY/OWASP/NIST refs present in the same result block; the checkout confirms every line-level fact (password: AtlasArgs.password().nullish() at createDBUser.ts:16-20, plain z.string() min 1 max 100 with no pattern at args.ts:74-76, the password echoed in the success response at 89-96 with the line-93 snippet verbatim, keychain registration at 84-87 that only feeds redaction of error messages (tool.ts:819), telemetry (telemetry.ts:342-348) and logs (loggerBase.ts:66) while the success path through invoke/appendUIResource performs no redaction), the stated compensating controls are real and accurately described (atlas-create-db-user is on the default confirmationRequiredTools list at userConfig.ts:83 and the prompt masks the password at line 109), nothing overrides the gap (deploy/ contains no readOnly or disabledTools settings), the repo is deployed in prod (partner exposure), qa and dev per env/*.json iac entries, the pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 matches the repo record, and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json:2399) so no lower severity is warranted; note for the keeper: the ledger already holds this exact fingerprint as open finding fnd_01M2G2AGTH64FMR4XR77ZAJH7B with the same target and ruleId (narrower location 84-96), so this append should update/supersede that record rather than create a second one.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All five cited instruments apply to example-co and are ordered Indian-first (sebi-cscrf-2024 is the primary instrument for a mid-size SEBI RE per details.json entityTypes stock-broker/depository-participant and active mid-size-re registrations; dpdp-rules-2025 is in frameworksInScope and covers stock-broker; owasp-asvs-5.0 and nist-800-53-r5 are cross-sector with empty applicability), controlIds sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S1 and dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) all exist in their catalog files and cover the credential-echo gap (PR.AA.S6's guidance names probe-schemas checking credentials and probe-schemas is in its probeWorkflows; 6(1) is the umbrella safeguards control with probe-schemas in its probeWorkflows and ledger precedent on this very app), and severity high is correctly derived as the catalog defaultSeverity of regulatoryRefs[0] PR.AA.S6 per maxwell-conventions section 4 with no CVSS/security-severity score present; the only repair is that the two global crosswalks owasp-asvs-5.0:13.3.1 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5(7) come from the schema-auditor agent's rule table and are not the catalog mappings[] of the cited control, which the regulatory-catalogs skill (section 2) requires crosswalks be taken from - PR.AA.S6's mappings list owasp-asvs-5.0:V6 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5, and the ledger's own PR.AA.S6 finding for this app cited exactly V6.).

title: connect tool accepts a MongoDB connection string with embedded credentials as a plain tool argument
description:
src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts:13-15 declares connectionString: z.string().describe("MongoDB connection string (in the mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// format)") with no pattern, format or secret marker; the mongodb+srv URI format embeds username:password, so the live credential is supplied through the LLM tool-call channel and persists in client transcripts. Line 43 passes it to this.session.connectToMongoDB({ connectionString }). Only config-supplied connection strings are registered for redaction (src/common/config/parseUserConfig.ts:179 and src/setup/setupMcpServer.ts:228); the tool-argument path never registers the string in the session keychain (verified: no keychain.register call on the connect path), so driver or parser error text that echoes the URI reaches the 30-day disk log unredacted. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every material claim was verified against files I opened: the SARIF export exists at the cited path and contains a SCH-API-06 result located at src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts with region startLine 13 endLine 48 and carrying the candidate's exact fingerprint aeaedeb4... (the 01→02→06→06 result ordering probes are consistent with the 'result index 3' locator); connect.ts:13-15 declares connectionString as a plain z.string() with no pattern, format or secret marker and line 43 passes it to session.connectToMongoDB; keychain.register appears only on the config path (parseUserConfig.ts:179, setupMcpServer.ts:228) and never on the tool path (error redaction via keychain.allSecrets therefore cannot scrub the URI); the disk logger is enabled by default with retentionDays 30 (userConfig.ts:58, diskLogger.ts:23); no ignore file or deployment override disables the connect tool (deploy/aws/Dockerfile disables only atlas-local, MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY explicitly keeps connect, server.json documents connect as the path when MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING is unset); the repo is deployed in dev/qa/prod (env records reference its Dockerfile/deploy IaC, prod partner-exposed with pii/financial data); severity high equals the verified catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 2399) and the export contains no security-severity override; all three controlIds exist as ledger control records (dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) applicable to the mcp-gateway environments) and the export's result properties carry the same controlIds; and the fingerprint is not already used in the ledger (the prior SCH-API-06 finding fnd_01M2G2AGTH64FMR4XR77ZAJH7B is a different instance at createDBUser.ts with a different fingerprint).); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All four cited instruments exist in the vocab and apply to example-co (SEBI CSCRF is in frameworksInScope and the company is an active SEBI mid-size-re stock-broker/DP, so the most specific Indian instrument is correctly first; DPDP Rules and the two cross-sector frameworks are applicability-legal), both SEBI controls exist in the SEBI catalog and their prose covers the credential-handling gap with severity high correctly derived as the catalog defaultSeverity of regulatoryRefs[0] sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (no CVE/CVSS or SARIF security-severity score basis exists, and the auditor's documented SCH-API-06 crosswalks are exactly owasp-asvs-5.0:13.3.1 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5(7), though the auditor's table maps this rule primarily to PR.AA.S1, which carries the same defaultSeverity), but the third ref dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) is mis-mapped and must be dropped: the DPDP catalog's own control 1 guidance forbids reporting rule 5-to-16 controls as current breaches before 13 May 2027 ("Until those dates neither the Act obligation nor the manner prescribed by these Rules is binding"), and 6(1)'s prose and guidance scope it to protecting personal data of Data Principals, which a MongoDB connection-string credential is not and which this finding never claims, so the mapping fails on that one ref yet is repaired by removing it, leaving a valid mapping on the in-force SEBI controls.).

title: switch-connection tool accepts a connection string with embedded credentials as a plain tool argument
description:
src/tools/mongodb/connect/switchConnection.ts:13-20 declares an optional connectionString: z.string() with no pattern and no secret marker (snippet: connectionString: z.string().optional().describe("MongoDB connection string to switch to (in the mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// format). If a connection string is not provided, the connection string from the config will be used.")) and line 51 passes it to this.session.connectToMongoDB without registering it in the session keychain - the same class of gap as the connect tool. Credentials supplied this way transit the LLM tool-call channel and persist in client transcripts; only the config-supplied connection string is redaction-registered. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every claim verified in files I opened: switchConnection.ts:13-20 declares connectionString: z.string().optional() with no pattern and no secret marker (the quoted describe snippet matches the checkout verbatim) and line 51 passes it to session.connectToMongoDB, which (session.ts:148-150) does no keychain registration while the only connection-string registration is the config-supplied one (parseUserConfig.ts:179), no override neutralises the tool (userConfig.ts disabledTools defaults to [], no allowlist), the repo is deployed in dev/qa/prod (prod exposure partner) with the same pattern in connect.ts (results[3] is its SCH-API-06 fail), the SARIF export's results[4] is a fail/error SCH-API-06 result located at switchConnection.ts region 13-57 whose message names switch-connection and the keychain, and severity high matches both the rule's severityBasis and catalog sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 defaultSeverity (cited PR.AA.S1 and dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) also exist, Indian instruments first); only the export's sha256 could not be recomputed (listed unverifiable; the export itself is present and contains the result, so the claim stands).); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All four cited instruments are in the vocab and applicable to example-co (sebi-cscrf-2024 covers its active stock-broker/depository-participant mid-size-re registrations and is correctly the first, most specific Indian instrument; dpdp-rules-2025 is in frameworksInScope with matching entityTypes; owasp-asvs-5.0 and nist-800-53-r5 are voluntary global crosswalks placed last and match the workflow's own SCH-API-06 rule table in .claude/agents/schema-auditor.md:186), all three control ids exist in their catalogs (PR.AA.S1 and PR.AA.S6 in sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json lines 2140/2393, 6(1) in dpdp-rules-2025.catalog.json line 564) and their prose/guidance cover the credential-management gap the checkout shows literally (switchConnection.ts:13-20 optional connectionString with no pattern or secret marker, line 51 passing it to connectToMongoDB with no keychain registration), and severity high follows maxwell-conventions section 4 step 2 exactly (no CVSS score present; PR.AA.S6 defaultSeverity is high, and the secondary PR.AA.S1 is also high so the value is stable whichever SEBI control is treated as most specific); two nuances that do not refute under this lens: DPDP Rule 6 commences only on 2027-05-13 per the registry structure note so the in-force anchor today would be dpdp-act-2023:8(5) (which the 6(1) catalog entry itself maps to), and the global crosswalks 13.3.1/IA-5(7) come from the schema-auditor rule table rather than the cited controls' catalog mappings (which list owasp-asvs-5.0:V6 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5), neither of which changes severity or applicability (SARIF rule/result internals beyond the first 2000 chars were unreadable, see unverifiable).)

title: export tool writes query results (pii, financial) to plaintext EJSON files with no encryption or access controls
description:
src/common/exportsManager.ts:198-249: ExportsManager.startExport does fs.mkdir(this.exportsDirectoryPath, { recursive: true }) then createWriteStream(inProgressExport.exportPath) - snippet: const outputStream = createWriteStream(inProgressExport.exportPath); const ejsonTransform = this.docToEJSONStream(...); await pipeline([input.stream(), ejsonTransform, outputStream]) - with no encryption, no file-mode restriction and no vault or KMS reference. The default folder is the user home .mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports directory (src/common/config/configUtils.ts:53-55) and each session writes under a per-session subfolder (lines 363-372). Files carry full find/aggregate documents from the client-data and order stores that env/prod.json classifies as pii and financial, are served back by resource URI and, when the server runs locally, by raw filesystem path (src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:119-124). Retention is a partial compensating control: exports expire after exportTimeoutMs (default 300000 ms, request overrides can only lower it) with a cleanup cycle (lines 297-338) and the folder is deleted recursively on shutdown (lines 110-126), but during their life the data sits unencrypted on the host. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1. DPDP Rule 6(1)(a) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: encryption. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passed on bytes I opened myself: the SARIF export at the cited path contains a SCH-PII-02 result at index 5 (confirmed by ruleId-chain probes: 5 ruleIds before it match, 6 do not) located at src/common/exportsManager.ts with startLine 198 and endLine 249, carrying the candidate's fingerprint value and the verbatim message phrase 'client-data and order stores', and its rule declares defaultSeverity high with severityBasis sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1; the checkout at pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 exhibits the gap exactly as described (createWriteStream with no mode option, no encryption or KMS/vault reference anywhere in the write path, exportsPath default ~/.mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports at configUtils.ts:53-55, per-session subfolder at 363-372, resource-URI and raw-path serving at export.ts:119-124, exportTimeoutMs default 300_000 with onlyLowerThanBaseValueOverride at userConfig.ts:194-198, cleanup at 297-338 and recursive shutdown deletion at 110-126), with no overriding compensating control in the repo (chmod/umask appear only in the src/ui frontend bundle and 'encrypt' only in atlas openapi.d.ts type declarations, neither in the export path), the condition is reachable in the deployed prod environment (env/prod.json dataClassification pii+financial, partner exposure) and independently corroborated by ledger observation obs_01M2H1VF3N8NATYT9XVASD12XF, severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.DS.S1 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3222, whose guidance prescribes high for unencrypted stores on the encryption topic) so no lower severity is supported, all cited controls exist and apply (RBI 140 is a Cryptographic Controls clause whose guidance names probe-schemas; dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(a) is a PR.DS.S1 catalog mapping; NIST SC-28 likewise), and the fingerprint is unused elsewhere in the ledger; the only unverifiable item is the export's sha256 digest (no independent record in the workspace to compare against), and evidence[1] is a byte-identical duplicate of evidence[0] minus its description.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every cited instrument binds example-co (sebi-cscrf-2024 via active mid-size-re stock-broker/DP registrations, rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 via the active nbfc-middle-layer registration and in force since 2026-07-31, dpdp-rules-2025 and the global nist-800-53-r5), each controlId exists in its catalog with prose covering unencrypted pii/financial data at rest — the PR.DS.S1 guidance prescribes exactly this finding ('Each unencrypted store ... is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1, topic encryption'), RBI 140's guidance names probe-schemas checking that sensitive fields are encrypted/tokenised, and 6(1)(a) mandates encryption of personal data — the most specific Indian instrument (SEBI, the company's primary licence and the ledger's existing SCH-PII-02 control key) is first with the global crosswalk last, and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.DS.S1 verified at sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3222 per maxwell-conventions section 4 (the finding carries no CVSS score and the tool's rule properties use defaultSeverity/severityBasis, not security-severity), with the 'readiness mapping' label on Rule 6(1)(a) matching the DPDP catalog's own commencement rule (rule 6 controls commence 2027-05-13; gaps before then are raised at catalog severity as readiness gaps) and 'SLA topic: encryption' being a valid vocab topic that the SEBI guidance says falls to the sla-table defaults. )

description: MCP server io.github.mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server v1.11.0 at commit aaa72a04 exposes 48 tools (19 write-capable) with readOnly defaulting to false, disabledTools defaulting to empty and a confirmation list covering only 8 write tools (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:74-103); the shipped AWS deploy config (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:13) disables only the atlas-local category. The elicitation confirmation gate itself fails open for clients without elicitation capability (src/elicitation.ts:30-44), so destructive tools (drop-database, delete-many, atlas-create-db-user, atlas-streams-manage and others) run without human approval against headless agent harnesses while aiCodingPolicy.humanReviewRequired is true. See findings AGENT-ASI09-01 and AGENT-ASI02-01 in the export.

title: HTTP MCP endpoint ships unauthenticated, unlimited and unwhitelisted
description: The streamable HTTP transport (src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319) validates only the optional httpHeaders map, which defaults to an empty object (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143); there is no OAuth, bearer or mTLS path and the server never terminates TLS itself. deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12-18 - the IaC the qa and prod environment records register - runs transport http on 0.0.0.0:8000 with MDB_MCP_EXTERNALLY_MANAGED_SESSIONS=true, no MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS and no readOnly. The transport also has no rate limiter and no session-count cap, and the connect and switch-connection tools accept connection strings with no host whitelist. See findings AGENT-MCP-01, AGENT-ASI08-03 and AGENT-ASI03-03.

evidence.description: lines 12-18: MDB_MCP_TRANSPORT=http, MDB_MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0, no auth headers
prod EKS ap-south-1, exposure partner, dataClassification pii+financial

title: Agent-serving MCP server has strong injection hygiene but a fail-open approval gate
description: The application-security posture of the agent-serving MCP server is mixed. Satisfied: every tool output carrying untrusted data is wrapped by formatUntrustedData with delimiting and an instruction-data separation warning (62 call sites, src/tools/tool.ts:967-994), tools have Zod input schemas, MCP readOnlyHint and destructiveHint annotations (src/tools/tool.ts:384-410), and tests/accuracy/untrustedData.test.ts exercises prompt-injection resistance. Gaps: the human-confirmation gate fails open (src/elicitation.ts:30-44) and the shipped AWS deployment runs the endpoint unauthenticated with all write tools enabled (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12-18).

evidence.description: pass results 10-12 (injection hygiene, secrets, annotations) and fail results 0-1

title: Deployed MCP server artifacts are not traceable to the pinned commit or an image record
description: The repo record pins commit aaa72a04 and environment records exist for dev, qa and prod, but the AWS deployment image installs mongodb-mcp-server@latest from the public registry on an unpinned node:24-alpine base (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2-9), so what runs in qa and prod cannot be tied to the audited commit; applications/mcp-gateway/images/ contains no image records (ledger observation obs_01M2H53C4VE2YHVQ9GFZM9AYYX already flags docker.io/mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server as untracked). server.json itself pins 1.11.0 for its own npm and OCI entries, which limits but does not close the gap for the deploy path actually registered.

evidence.description: obs_01M2H53C4VE2YHVQ9GFZM9AYYX: no image records for mcp-gateway

title: Unpinned installs of the MCP server and unverified third-party skill content
description: Three supply-chain gaps break software integrity for the agent platform: the AWS deploy image installs mongodb-mcp-server@latest on an unpinned base (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2-9); the setup wizard writes npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@latest into six harness MCP configs (src/setup/aiTool.ts:195-205, 418-429), re-resolving the registry at every harness start; and the skills flow runs npx --yes skills@1 add mongodb/agent-skills -y -g (src/setup/installSkills.ts:39-41), installing model-steering prompt content by branch reference with no hash, signature or commit pinning. Mitigations present: pnpm-lock.yaml for the repo build and server.json pins 1.11.0 for its own published entries.

evidence.description: lockfile present for the repo build

title: Redaction exists but model-controlled connections and unredacted assistant egress open leak paths
description: Satisfied elements: tool errors are redacted via keychain and mongodb-redact (src/tools/tool.ts:813-829), telemetry events are redacted before sending, and untrusted data in tool output is delimited. Leak paths remain: connect and switch-connection accept arbitrary mongodb:// URIs from the model with no host allow-list (src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts:13-17, switchConnection.ts:13-20), so a hijacked agent can redirect queries and exports to an attacker-chosen host; and search-knowledge POSTs the model-composed query verbatim to knowledge.mongodb.com with no redaction (src/tools/assistant/searchKnowledge.ts:59-64).

evidence.description: handleError redacts raw error messages with session.keychain.allSecrets

title: IN-resident Atlas service but ungated egress to global MongoDB endpoints from a pii+financial gateway
description: The approved vendor service (mongodb-atlas, atlas-mumbai) hosts the data in AWS ap-south-1 with IN residency, and the environment records declare residency IN. However the assistant tool category and telemetry egress to knowledge.mongodb.com and cloud.mongodb.com are enabled by default (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:25-29, 113-117), are not disabled in the shipped deploy config, and carry model-context data (the natural-language search query) with no redaction or data-class gate, while aiCodingPolicy.allowedDataClasses permits only public and internal for AI tooling.

evidence.description: atlas-mumbai service, hostingCountries IN, dataAccessed pii+financial

title: Loopback default with exposure warning, undermined by the deploy config and unrestricted connect tools
description: The HTTP transport defaults to binding 127.0.0.1 (userConfig.ts:131-135) and logs an explicit security warning when asked to bind wider addresses (src/transports/streamableHttp.ts:156-160, 242-249). However the shipped AWS deployment binds 0.0.0.0 unauthenticated (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:17), the Azure bicep default is NOAUTH with external ingress (deploy/azure/bicep/main.bicep:48-53, 151-156), and the connect and switch-connection tools let the model steer the session to arbitrary hosts with no egress allow-list, so network segmentation of the agent surface is not enforced.

evidence.description: authMode default NOAUTH, ingress external true

title: Repo carries developer-harness configuration outside aiCodingPolicy.harnessesAllowed
description: The audited checkout ships harness configuration for GitHub Copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/agents/agentic-workflows.agent.md, .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml) and .vscode/, none of which is on the SDLC policy allow-list of claude-code and opencode; the agentic-workflows agent file additionally instructs that bash tools remain enabled by default without restriction, against the policy promptInjectionControls of tool-allowlist and human-approval-for-writes. This is upstream developer-harness configuration (engineers working on the repo), distinct from the deployed gateway. The deployed MCP gateway itself is within the SDLC policy scope; the harness-allow-list violation is recorded as finding AGENT-POL-01.

title: Tool-call logging exists with secret redaction but no server-enforced retention
description: The server ships disk, mcp and stderr loggers (userConfig.ts:47-63), logs tool executions at debug level (src/tools/tool.ts:514-543), attributes the sessionId on the HTTP transport (src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:263), and redacts secrets from log and error output via keychain and mongodb-redact. The server itself enforces no retention or rotation policy for the disk logger; platform records declare logsRetentionDays 365 (prod) and 180 (qa) with logsInIndia true, but the dev environment declares 30 days, below the CERT-In 180-day floor. SLA topic: log-retention.

evidence.description: disk logger, no retention or rotation policy in-repo

title: Scoping mechanisms exist but the shipped attack surface is the full 48-tool default-on set
description: The server anticipates agent attack vectors well (untrusted-data framing, annotations, one-way readOnly override, request-override restrictions with allowRequestOverrides default false, secret redaction, injection evals), but the shipped deployment exposes the maximum surface: 48 tools on by default including drop-database and Atlas cluster administration, unauthenticated HTTP on 0.0.0.0, externally managed sessions, and a confirmation gate that fails open. The reference harness architecture (egress classes, *_paused brakes, per-run budgets) is not implemented for this gateway.

evidence.description: server manifest: full tool and env surface

title: Algorithmic due diligence partially performed for the agent-facing MCP gateway
description: The upstream project ships genuine due-diligence artefacts for an algorithmic system: accuracy test suites across 40+ tool tests (tests/accuracy/), a prompt-injection corpus (tests/accuracy/untrustedData.test.ts), strict Zod input schemas per tool, and MCP tool annotations. The deployed configuration was not given the equivalent due diligence: it runs the pii+financial gateway with write tools unapproved-by-default-off, no authentication on the HTTP endpoint and a fail-open approval gate, per findings AGENT-ASI09-01, AGENT-ASI02-01 and AGENT-MCP-01.

title: Model-facing tools can write pii and financial records with no access scoping by default
description: The gateway serves client-data stores classified pii and financial (env records), yet update-many, insert-many, rename-collection, create-collection and create-index are callable with no human approval, readOnly is default false, disabledTools is default empty, and the HTTP MCP endpoint accepting those calls is unauthenticated in the shipped deploy config. A prompt-injected or hijacked agent can therefore bulk-modify personal and financial records with no effective access-control boundary between the model and the data. Finding AGENT-ASI02-01.

title: Assistant and telemetry egress to global MongoDB endpoints ungated from an IN-residency workload
description: Personal data processed by the gateway sits in IN-resident Atlas clusters per the vendor record, but the search-knowledge tool POSTs the model-composed query - which can embed client PII from the agent context - verbatim to knowledge.mongodb.com (assistantBaseUrl default, src/common/config/userConfig.ts:25-29) with no redaction, no data-class filter and no gating, and telemetry (default enabled) sends event metadata to cloud.mongodb.com. Neither channel is disabled or restricted in the shipped deploy config, and no transfer assessment exists for these endpoints. Finding AGENT-ASI03-04; SLA topic: data-localisation.

evidence.description: callAssistantApi posts to assistantBaseUrl with no redaction

title: MCP gateway inventoried but no architecture-level egress or approval taxonomy
description: For the NBFC arm (nbfc-middle-layer registration), the emerging-technology adoption is partially architected: the gateway is inventoried as an application with pinned repo, environments, vendor and env records, and the server exposes a coherent declarative config surface (userConfig.ts with per-field override semantics). Missing at the architecture level: no egress class taxonomy (offline, loopback-only, governed), no declared approval taxonomy for tool categories (the confirmation list is a flat tool-name list), and no runtime brake or pause flag for the agent surface.

evidence.description: declarative config surface with override behaviours

title: MCP gateway adopted for a critical function with gaps above the stated risk appetite
description: The gateway supports the order-routing critical function and processes pii and financial data, but the audited configuration carries gaps whose catalog severities (high, per the cited SEBI controls) exceed the company risk appetite of maxAcceptableSeverity medium: fail-open human approval, unauthenticated HTTP transport in the deploy config, unpinned install paths, default-on write tools and no rate limiting. Resilience budgets exist at the query level (maxBytesPerQuery, maxDocumentsPerQuery, idleTimeoutMs) but not at the endpoint level.

evidence.description: riskAppetite.maxAcceptableSeverity medium; order-routing critical function lists mcp-gateway

title: Secure coding and testing strong; secure deployment configuration weak
description: Threat modelling for prompt injection is present (untrusted-data framing, injection evals, secret redaction, Zod validation, annotations), but the secure-deployment half fails: the shipped AWS image installs the server unpinned over the public registry on an unpinned base (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:2-9) and runs the endpoint unauthenticated with write tools enabled. Findings AGENT-ASI04-01 and AGENT-MCP-01.

title: Evaluated upstream artefacts exist; the deployed configuration was not evaluated for prod use
description: The MCP server itself is a known version (1.11.0, pinned in server.json and the repo record) from an approved vendor (mongodb-atlas, materiality material, last assessment 2026-06-15 rating medium), and the project ships evaluation suites. What was not evaluated before prod use is the deployment configuration this audit found unauthenticated and unpinned, indicating the pre-adoption security evaluation did not cover the deploy path or the agent-facing hardening.

evidence.description: server version 1.11.0, npm and OCI entries pinned

title: Platform retention meets 180 days in prod and qa but not dev; server enforces no retention
description: The environment records declare logsRetentionDays 365 (prod) and 180 (qa) with logsInIndia true, satisfying the 180-day retention floor at the platform level for the deployed tiers; the dev environment declares 30 days and the MCP server's own disk logger has no retention or rotation policy, so retention depends entirely on platform configuration. SLA topic: log-retention.

title: MongoDB MCP confirmation gate fails open: destructive tools execute without human approval
description: src/elicitation.ts:31-33: `if (!this.supportsElicitation()) { return true; }` - Elicitation.requestConfirmation returns true whenever the connected MCP client does not advertise elicitation capability, so the eight destructive tools gated by the default confirmationRequiredTools (drop-database, drop-collection, delete-many, drop-index, atlas-create-access-list, atlas-create-db-user, atlas-streams-manage, atlas-streams-teardown) execute with no human confirmation against elicitation-incapable clients, which includes common headless agent harnesses. ToolBase.verifyConfirmed (src/tools/tool.ts:609-615) delegates the entire approval gate to this method, and the default config (userConfig.ts:79-94) defines no other approval path. This is the deployed agent gateway for app mcp-gateway (qa and prod, EKS ap-south-1, partner exposure, data classes pii and financial, supports the order-routing critical function) and sdlc/policy.json aiCodingPolicy.humanReviewRequired is true. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S3. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every material claim verifies in files I opened: src/elicitation.ts:31-33 returns true whenever the client cannot elicit, src/tools/tool.ts:491-515 and 609-615 show this is the only approval gate for the exactly-eight default confirmationRequiredTools listed at src/common/config/userConfig.ts:79-94, no deployed override compensates (deploy/aws/Dockerfile - the qa/prod IaC root per env/qa.json, env/prod.json - disables only atlas-local and sets no MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY, and the azure bicep's readOnly default is overridden to "false" in both parameter templates), qa and prod exist on EKS ap-south-1 with pii/financial data classes (prod partner-exposed; qa is internal, a harmless compression in the description's parenthetical), details.json maps the order-routing critical function to mcp-gateway, sdlc/policy.json has aiCodingPolicy.humanReviewRequired true, the checkout .git/HEAD equals the pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0, the SARIF export exists and contains the AGENT-ASI09-01 rule and a result with ruleId AGENT-ASI09-01 at src/elicitation.ts startLine 30 carrying the identical fingerprint f658ce80...cb0f0, and severity high equals both the SARIF rule's and the sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S3 catalog defaultSeverity (line 2249); evidence[1] is a bare duplicate of evidence[0] but both entries resolve and support the claim, so it is redundant rather than refuting.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All three cited instruments apply to example-co and are correctly ordered - sebi-cscrf-2024 (active mid-size-re stock-broker/DP, in frameworksInScope) first with PR.AA.S3 (catalog prose 'Least Privilege ... along with segregation of duties', the auditor's prescribed mapping for AGENT-ASI09-01, defaultSeverity high matching the candidate's severity since no CVSS or SARIF security-severity score exists on the candidate or the rule, and the rule's error level would also map high so the generic-lens vs skill ordering discrepancy is immaterial), then owasp-agentic-top10-2026 ASI09 (trust exploitation, matching the single asi09 tag and the fails-open human-approval weakness on regulated destructive actions with humanReviewRequired true, not ASI02 which is about missing allow-lists/scoping) and owasp-llm-top10-2025 LLM06 (excessive agency: 'require human approval for high-impact actions') - all three ids exist (SEBI catalog / registry structures for the catalog-less OWASP instruments) with regulator pairings matching the registry, so no correction is needed (unverifiable: the SARIF results array beyond the first 2000 characters - single-line export truncated by the reader and grep is blind to the gitignored kpis/data/raw tree - but the rule definition and every mapping input were confirmed).).

title: HTTP MCP transport deployed unauthenticated on 0.0.0.0 in the AWS deploy path
description: deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12-18 sets `ENV MDB_MCP_TRANSPORT=http`, `MDB_MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `MDB_MCP_EXTERNALLY_MANAGED_SESSIONS=true` and no MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS, MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY or confirmation list. The transport it enables validates only the configured httpHeaders map, which defaults to an empty object (src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319: `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders))`, with userConfig.ts:136-143 `.default({})`), so every request is accepted: no OAuth, no bearer validation, no mTLS, and the server never terminates TLS itself. This is the deployment path the qa and prod environment records register (iac: deploy) for environments classified pii and financial with partner exposure, so all 48 tools - including drop-database and Atlas administration - are reachable unauthenticated on the network. CSA MCP security practices guide 8.3 (authentication). Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S17. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every material claim is verified in files I opened myself: deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12-18 sets exactly ENV MDB_MCP_TRANSPORT=http, MDB_MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0 and MDB_MCP_EXTERNALLY_MANAGED_SESSIONS=true with no MDB_MCP_HTTP_HEADERS, MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY or confirmation env anywhere in the file, src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319 gates requests only on Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders) which src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143 defaults to {} (and no TLS or other auth middleware exists in src/transports), env/qa.json and env/prod.json both register this repo's deploy root under iac[] for pii/financial workloads, no compensating or overriding control exists in the repo (only Azure bicep auth templates on the unregistered Azure path and server.json schema docs), severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S17 which applies to this SEBI mid-size RE, and the 48-tool inventory (24 mongodb + 18 atlas + 4 atlas-local + 2 assistant, including DropDatabaseTool and the Atlas administration tools) is exact, while the cited SARIF export exists, parses, and its rules[] carries AGENT-MCP-01 with the candidate's byte-identical defaultSeverity, regulatoryRefs and tags - but its results[] array and sha256 could not be opened because the single-line export is gitignored (.gitignore:11) and beyond the read tool's 2000-char per-line limit, so those are listed under unverifiable rather than counted against the candidate, with two wording imprecisions returned as corrections.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Not refuted: sebi-cscrf-2024 is the most specific Indian instrument for this SEBI mid-size RE (active stock-broker/DP registrations, mid-size-re category, first in frameworksInScope) and is cited first; PR.AA.S17 exists in the SEBI catalog, applies to mid-size REs (not exempted), and its prose (API security with proper authentication and authorisation, access management so only intended entities reach APIs, whitelist-based connectivity) directly covers the unauthenticated 0.0.0.0 HTTP MCP transport I confirmed myself in deploy/aws/Dockerfile:12-18, src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319 and src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143 (.default({})); severity high correctly derives from PR.AA.S17's catalog defaultSeverity (no CVSS, CVE or security-severity score exists on the SARIF rule, whose level error maps to high anyway), the OWASP Agentic ref ASI03 matches the owasp-agentic-top10-2026:asi03 tag and the identity/privilege-abuse weakness described (unauthenticated access, not ASI01/02/04), LLM06 (excessive agency, 48 tools incl. drop-database unauthenticated) and CSA 8.3 (registry instructs citing 8.3 with the practice named) are valid registry ids cited as sanctioned secondary crosswalks exactly as PR.AA.S17's own guidance prescribes for probe-agent-graph, and the sebi-cscrf-2024 patch-sla high row (7 days) exists for the claimed topic; one wording nit that does not affect the mapping: qa.json is exposure "internal", so "partner exposure" strictly holds only for the prod environment.).

title: AWS deploy image installs the MCP server unpinned at registry latest
description: deploy/aws/Dockerfile:9: `RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest` on an unpinned base at line 2 `FROM node:24-alpine` (no digest); ARG VERSION=latest feeds only a LABEL. The artifact that runs in the deployed gateway therefore depends on whatever the public registry serves at build time and cannot be traced to the audited commit aaa72a04; no image records exist for mcp-gateway (ledger obs_01M2H53C4VE2YHVQ9GFZM9AYYX). server.json pins 1.11.0 for its own npm and OCI entries, but this deploy path bypasses that pin and violates dependencyPolicy.lockfilesRequired. Deployed configuration for qa and prod (pii and financial, order-routing critical function). Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passed on files I opened: the checkout's deploy/aws/Dockerfile shows exactly the claimed gap (line 2 FROM node:24-alpine with no digest, line 3 ARG VERSION=latest feeding only the LABEL at line 24, line 9 hardcoded RUN npm install -g mongodb-mcp-server@latest), the cited SARIF export exists and contains an AGENT-ASI04-01 result at deploy/aws/Dockerfile with region startLine 2 endLine 9 whose message cites mongodb-mcp-server@latest and node:24-alpine (verified by bounded co-occurrence probes on the single-line export, which holds exactly one deploy/aws/Dockerfile uri), the rule's own metadata carries defaultSeverity high with SEBI sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6 as first regulatoryRef matching the catalog defaultSeverity high, the gap is not overridden (the @latest install ignores ARG VERSION, deploy/aws/README.md itself builds and pushes :latest to ECR, the bicep 1.11.0 tag pin covers only the azure path, and the only sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 ledger control record is implementationStatus unknown / effectiveness ineffective) and is reachable because env/qa.json and env/prod.json both register this repo's deploy path as iac for pii/financial workloads behind the order-routing critical function, so severity high is justified and nothing supports lowering it; the sha256 is unverifiable (no other record of that digest exists in the workspace) and the evidence[0] locator 'result 2' could not be byte-confirmed though ruleId, path and lines match, which I treat as a transcription slip per the caller's instruction; also flagged for the other lenses: the open ledger finding fnd_01M2HCWMBDBP41GF0TNY5731M8 (probe-iac) already covers this same gap with a different fingerprint, and sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6's catalog applicability [mii, qualified-re] does not intersect this mid-size-re (this run's refresh-soc inventory marked it not-applicable) - a regulatory-mapping question outside the evidence lens.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The mapping is repairable, so not refuted, but as written the primary control sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6 does not bind this company - its catalog applicability is reCategories [mii, qualified-re] with prose 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs' while details.json records both SEBI registrations as mid-size-re - rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:83 excludes nbfc from its applicability ('Not carried into the NBFC Directions') while the company's only RBI category is nbfc-middle-layer, and csa-mcp-security-2025:8.3's recorded practices (tool-call authorisation, argument validation, human confirmation, secrets) do not cover install-time pinning; the repair is sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5 (applies to all REs, covers the untraceable deployed artifact with no image record/SBOM per its own guidance, defaultSeverity high so severity high stands), retaining owasp-agentic-top10-2026:ASI04 (matches the asi04 tag and the unpinned-MCP-server weakness per the registry's ASI04 hard requirement) and nist-ssdf-800-218:PW.4.1 (valid id covering acquisition of verified components; a mappings-sourced alternative is PS.3.2 from GV.SC.S5's mappings).).

title: Setup wizard writes npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@latest into six harness MCP configs
description: src/setup/aiTool.ts:196-205: `const args = ["-y", "mongodb-mcp-server@latest"]; return { command: "npx", args, env }` (and the OpenCode variant at lines 418-429). The wizard writes this entry into Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and OpenCode MCP configs, so developer agents launch whatever the registry serves, re-resolved at every harness start, bypassing the pinned commit and pnpm-lock.yaml of this checkout. Developer-harness configuration running on dev laptops for engineers working on the mcp-gateway app. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Not refuted: the pinned checkout exhibits exactly the claimed gap - src/setup/aiTool.ts:195-205 hardcodes args ["-y","mongodb-mcp-server@latest"] under command "npx" (OpenCode override at 418-429, all six harnesses in AI_TOOL_REGISTRY:440-447, the write path live via setupMcpServer.ts:124 and the package.json setup bin), no pinning overlay, ignore file or compensating control exists anywhere in the repo (18 mongodb-mcp-server@ matches and none pins a reviewed version for the wizard; README, deploy/aws/Dockerfile:9 and docker.yml:39 compound it, and pnpm-lock.yaml cannot govern the npx-resolved package), developer-harness reachability is grounded in applications/mcp-gateway/env/dev.json hosting.accountRef "developer-laptops", severity high equals sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6's catalog defaultSeverity exactly as claimed, and the cited SARIF export exists and its readable portion carries tool maxwell-agent-graph-auditor 1.0.0 and rule AGENT-ASI04-01; the export's results[] body beyond character 2000 could not be read (single-line gitignored file: read truncates at 2000 chars, grep skips ignored *.export.json, file:// fetch rejected) so the exact result-3 entry and its sha256 are listed unverifiable rather than contradicted, the description's quoted `return { command: "npx", args, env }` is a benign paraphrase of the literal args array at line 202 (the base implementation silently drops the pushed --readOnly - a separate issue worth its own probe), and one cross-lens note: PR.DS.S6's catalog applicability lists reCategories [mii, qualified-re] while details.json records mid-size-re, and rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 controls are recorded not-applicable for this company elsewhere in the ledger, which the regulatory-mapping lens should confirm.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The primary ref cites sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6, but that catalog control's applicability.reCategories is [mii, qualified-re] and its prose exempts Mid-size REs, while details.json registers example-co as an active mid-size-re; and the secondary ref cites rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:83, whose applicability.entityTypes excludes nbfc and whose guidance states it is 'Not carried into the NBFC Directions' while the company's only RBI registration is nbfc-middle-layer - both Indian mappings are wrong but repairable, so correctedRegulatoryRefs substitute sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S2 (mid-size-applicable, covers third-party components of information systems being identified and assessed, defaultSeverity medium, matching the devenv-auditor's mapping for the same unpinned-npx-MCP-server weakness) and rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:31 (applies to nbfc-middle-layer per NBFC Directions para 87, guidance names probe-agent-graph for agent tooling), with correctedSeverity medium since maxwell-conventions section 4 derives severity from the catalog defaultSeverity of regulatoryRefs[0] and no CVSS/security-severity score exists (the auditor's SARIF emission spec puts only properties.defaultSeverity on rules); the OWASP ASI04 ref correctly matches the owasp-agentic-top10-2026:asi04 tag and the unpinned-MCP-server weakness, and NIST PW.4.1 and CSA 8.3 stand.).

title: Setup installs third-party agent skills globally with no integrity check
description: src/setup/installSkills.ts:39-41: `["--yes", SKILLS_CLI_PIN, "add", SKILLS_REPO, "--agent", agentId, "-y", "-g"]` with SKILLS_REPO = mongodb/agent-skills and SKILLS_CLI_PIN = skills@1. The command installs skill and prompt content that steers the harness model globally (-g) from a GitHub repository referenced by branch, not by commit, hash or signature; only the skills CLI package is pinned to major version 1. The flow is offered after a single interactive confirm for cursor, github-copilot, windsurf, claude-code and opencode, and no hash or signature verification of the fetched skill content exists anywhere in the setup path. Developer-harness configuration on dev machines for engineers of the mcp-gateway app. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.DS.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every material claim checks out against bytes I opened: the checkout's src/setup/installSkills.ts:39-41 matches the quoted `--yes skills@1 add mongodb/agent-skills --agent <id> -y -g` verbatim with no hash/signature verification anywhere in the setup path, aiTool.ts confirms exactly the five named agents (cursor, github-copilot, windsurf, claude-code, opencode) behind a single interactive confirm, setupMcpServer.ts:489 wires the flow, env/dev.json places it on the developer-laptops dev tier where it runs, and the cited SARIF export exists and contains the AGENT-ASI04-02 result at src/setup/installSkills.ts:31-41 with the candidate's exact fingerprint value, rule defaultSeverity high and result level error - matching the sebi-cscrf-2024 catalog defaultSeverity of PR.DS.S6 (high), so severity high is justified and no lower severity is supported; one observation for the regulatory-mapping pass, not an evidence defect: the catalog restricts PR.DS.S6 to reCategories mii/qualified-re while example-co is a mid-size-re (the OWASP ASI04 'agentic supply chain' mapping fits per the instruments registry, and the CSA 8.3 citation mirrors the auditor rule's own metadata); the export's sha256 and the 'result 4' ordinal are unverifiable as noted.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (The only Indian ref, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S6, is catalog-applicability mii/qualified-re only with prose 'Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26)' while example-co is an active mid-size-re, so the primary clause cannot bind this company - but the mapping is repairable with sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S1 (mandatory for all REs, 'deploying only hardened and vetted' software, defaultSeverity high so severity high stands), and every other check passes: the SEBI, OWASP and CSA instruments apply with matching regulators, the OWASP ASI04 ref matches the asi04 tag and the agentic-supply-chain weakness I confirmed in the checkout (SKILLS_REPO by branch, skills@1, -g, no hash/signature), the most specific Indian instrument is first, and patch-sla is the correct topic; note the CSA 8.3 secondary ref is retained as a broad voluntary crosswalk though the auditor's own ASI04-02 row lists no crosswalk, so the caller may drop it.).

Unconfirmed write tools include update-many (bulk modify with upsert), insert-many, rename-collection, create-collection, create-index, atlas-upgrade-cluster, atlas-create-free-cluster, atlas-create-project, atlas-streams-build and the atlas-local create and delete deployment tools. The shipped deploy config (deploy/aws/Dockerfile:13) disables only the atlas-local category, so a model can bulk-modify pii and financial client records in qa and prod. Per-tool parameter validation is present (Zod argsShape on every tool), so the gap is the absent least-privilege default, not input validation; aiCodingPolicy.promptInjectionControls names tool-allowlist and human-approval-for-writes but the deployed configuration implements neither for this gateway. the repo has 19 write-capable tools (9 mongodb, 8 atlas, 2 atlas-local; operationType spot-checked on update-many "update" and atlas-streams-build "create", Zod argsShape present) of which exactly the 11 the description lists name-for-name are unconfirmed; deploy/aws/Dockerfile:13 overrides only MDB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS=atlas-local (the root Dockerfile sets no tool limits, the azure bicep MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY:'true' template is not the AWS path the env records deploy, and the repo contains no settings.json/permission-map scoping that would exempt the rule); qa (internal) and prod (partner) both deploy this repo's deploy path with pii+financial data and aiCodingPolicy.promptInjectionControls matches sdlc/policy.json; the SARIF export exists at the cited path as the maxwell-agent-graph-auditor 1.0.0 log and contains a result with "ruleId":"AGENT-ASI02-01" whose own object carries a userConfig location with startLine 74 and endLine 103, a message discussing confirmationRequiredTools, and the workflow-computed fingerprint 5e8d5ad607ba7b8c4f85364640afdeca826d84ab45d32b497c7dba48e91dfb3d, its sha256 matching the digest attested in the auditor's own session transcript; severity high equals the sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S3 catalog defaultSeverity (catalog line 2249) and the evidence supports it, so no lower severity is warranted.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All five cited instruments apply (SEBI CSCRF binds the mid-size-re stock broker/DP and is first, DPDP Rules 2025 covers stock-brokers and is second, the OWASP/CSA frameworks are cross-sector and prescribed for LLM-agent companies by the skill's selection table), every controlId exists and its text covers the gap (PR.AA.S3 least privilege, DPDP 6(1)(b) access control with the tools-reach-personal-data condition met, ASI02 tool-misuse matching the asi02 tag and the over-broad-tool-side-effects weakness, LLM06 excessive agency, CSA 8.3 allowlist/human-confirmation practices named in the finding), and severity high is correctly derived per maxwell-conventions section 4 since the SARIF export carries no security-severity and the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S3 is high, with the gap confirmed in userConfig.ts:74-103 and deploy/aws/Dockerfile:13.).

title: connect and switch-connection accept model-controlled connection strings with no host allow-list
description: src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts:14: `connectionString: z.string().describe("MongoDB connection string (in the mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// format)")` (and switchConnection.ts:13-20). The value is passed to session.connectToMongoDB and on to the driver with no host allow-list or scheme enforcement (src/common/session.ts:148, src/common/connectionManager.ts). A hijacked or prompt-injected agent can redirect the session - and every subsequent find, aggregate, export or insert call - to an attacker-chosen host, exfiltrating client data from the gateway network position or pointing the gateway at an unapproved cluster; connect-type tools also stay enabled in readOnly mode. No egress class (offline, loopback-only, governed) is declared or enforced anywhere in the server, against the reference harness architecture requirement. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024 PR.AA.S2. SLA topic: patch-sla. title: mcp-gateway/mongodb-mcp-server: Human-confirmation gate for destructive MCP tools fails open for clients without elicitation support
description:
ASVS 5.0 L2 scope with agent-code lenses (LLM06, ASI02). destructive tools (drop-database, drop-collection, delete-many, drop-index, atlas-create-db-user, atlas-create-access-list, atlas-streams-manage, atlas-streams-teardown) are listed in confirmationRequiredTools by default (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:79-94) and ToolBase.invoke asks Elicitation.requestConfirmation before executing them (src/tools/tool.ts:491-513, 609-615); requestConfirmation returns true immediately when the MCP client does not declare the elicitation capability (src/elicitation.ts:30-33), so any client that omits that capability executes destructive operations against the pii/financial stores with no human approval. ExampleCo sdlc policy lists human-approval-for-writes as its prompt-injection control, and this is the code path meant to enforce it. Severity high from the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S3 (least privilege and segregation of duties); no CVSS computed because the caller already reaches the API - the defect removes a required human control rather than crossing a privilege boundary. SARIF result index 1.

Data flow: tools/call on MCP HTTP transport -> ToolBase.invoke requiresConfirmation (tool.ts:491-513) -> verifyConfirmed -> Elicitation.requestConfirmation returns true when supportsElicitation() is false (elicitation.ts:31-33) -> destructive tool executes against MongoDB

Exploit scenario: An MCP client (for example a compromised or prompt-injected agent runtime) sends initialize without the elicitation capability, then calls tools/call drop-database; the server skips the confirmation entirely and drops the database with no human ever seeing a prompt.

Impact: On the partner-exposed prod gateway every confirmation-required destructive operation is effectively unattended for clients that omit one capability flag, defeating the human-approval-for-writes control of the company AI coding policy for a system holding pii and financial data; a prompt-injected agent (LLM06/ASI02) can destroy or rewrite client data before a human notices. Catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S3 is high; recorded as context, not as an uplift.

Remediation: Fail closed: in Elicitation.requestConfirmation, return false (refuse the call) when the client does not support elicitation while a confirmation-required tool is invoked; optionally add a config flag to make confirmations mandatory for destructive tools regardless of client capability, and log every confirmation request and outcome as a security event.

Source: maxwell-secure-code-reviewer agent analysis (execute-scr) at pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0; no scanner SARIF log exists for this target.

title: mcp-gateway/mongodb-mcp-server: Telemetry enabled by default sends machine and usage identifiers to the MongoDB cloud with no consent gate
description:
ASVS 5.0 L2 scope, data-protection lens. Telemetry defaults to enabled (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:113-117); the Telemetry pipeline batches events every 30 seconds and posts them, after keychain redaction of secret values, to the MongoDB cloud endpoint api/private/unauth/telemetry/events under https://cloud.mongodb.com (src/common/atlas/apiClient.ts:170-236), with a fallback to the unauthenticated endpoint whenever the Atlas token is absent or rejected. Events carry device_id sourced from node-machine-id machineId(true) (src/helpers/deviceId.ts:20-24), session_id, tool names, durations, result status, Atlas project and org ids and auth types (src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:339-352; src/tools/atlas/atlasTool.ts:97-129); the only opt-outs are the DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable or telemetry disabled in config, neither set by deploy/aws/Dockerfile. No consent notice, purpose artefact or processor agreement is consulted before this external disclosure from an IN-residency deployment. Severity medium from the catalog defaultSeverity of dpdp-rules-2025:3 (standalone, itemised consent notice). Confidence likely: the egress and defaults are confirmed in code, but whether the machine identifier constitutes personal data and any DPA with MongoDB are not visible in the repo. SARIF result index 2.

Data flow: tool/server events -> Telemetry.emitEvents (telemetry.ts:209-215) -> sendEvents with redacted properties (telemetry.ts:339-352) -> ApiClient.sendUnauthEvents POST to https://cloud.mongodb.com api/private/unauth/telemetry/events (apiClient.ts:218-236), device_id from node-machine-id (deviceId.ts:20-24)

Exploit scenario: Deploy the shipped defaults (deploy/aws/Dockerfile sets no MDB_MCP_TELEMETRY) on the prod gateway; from the first tool call the deployment continuously emits the EKS node machine identifier, session ids, tool usage and Atlas project ids to MongoDB servers outside the company boundary, with no notice to or consent artefact for the company and no processor agreement visible in the repo.

Impact: Default-on external disclosure of persistent device identifiers and gateway usage metadata from a system processing pii and financial data for an Indian SEBI/RBI-regulated entity with dataResidency IN; DPDP Rules 2025 require an itemised consent notice before such sharing and the SDLC secrets policy expects AWS Secrets Manager for credentials, not ad-hoc third-party telemetry. Catalog defaultSeverity of dpdp-rules-2025:3 is medium; recorded as context, not as an uplift.

Remediation: Set MDB_MCP_TELEMETRY=disabled (or DO_NOT_TRACK) in the mcp-gateway deployments and consider changing the upstream default to disabled for enterprise deployments; if telemetry is retained, document a purpose and processor agreement with MongoDB, hash the machine identifier, and gate emission on a recorded consent decision.

Source: maxwell-secure-code-reviewer agent analysis (execute-scr) at pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0; no scanner SARIF log exists for this target.

title: db-models/onfinance-db-model-master: Cleartext broker credentials modelled in the secrets MongoDB collection
description:
onfinance_db_model_master/models.py:8-15 (Secrets Document) declares apiKey, zerodha_username, zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa, apiSecrets, accessToken and accountName as plain StringField, so any service that persists this model stores Zerodha broker login credentials, the TOTP 2FA seed, API secrets and access tokens unencrypted in the db-models-mongodb.default.secrets MongoDB collection. company-profile/example-co/sdlc/metastore.json classifies zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa, apiSecrets and accessToken as restricted and spdi personal data, and policy.json requires secrets in aws-secrets-manager (90-day rotation), which this model bypasses by design. The same root cause covers the user collection: user_password BinaryField (models.py:390) and user_binance_auth_creds DynamicField (models.py:397); one fix covers both locations. Reviewed at commit 70b3633e171a1b8d389b27bb901c84c34a0e9bf6; SARIF result ruleId asvs-v14-sensitive-storage (fail). SLA topic: encryption.

Data flow: Secrets Document fields (apiKey, zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa, apiSecrets, accessToken as StringField, models.py:8-15) -> mongoengine Document persistence -> db-models-mongodb.default.secrets collection stored in cleartext; same pattern user_password models.py:390 and user_binance_auth_creds models.py:397 -> user collection

Exploit scenario: An attacker with read access to the db-models-mongodb instance (dev database, or a consuming-service backup, export or staging copy of these collections) reads zerodha_password, zerodha_2fa and accessToken values verbatim with no decryption or cracking, then authenticates to the linked brokerage account as the record owner by replaying the password plus the 2FA seed and calls the broker API with the plaintext accessToken.

Impact: Disclosure of restricted SPDI credentials for every record persisted through this model: broker password, 2FA seed, API secret and access token exposure is direct account takeover of the linked brokerage account, not just data disclosure, and a reportable personal-data breach for this SEBI broker and RBI NBFC. Context that does not lower severity: db-models runs in the dev tier with isolated exposure and no network entry points of its own, and the catalog severity high of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1 stands for an unencrypted store carrying regulatory data regardless of tier.

Remediation: Move credential values to the policy secrets backend (aws-secrets-manager per company-profile/example-co/sdlc/policy.json secretsManagement.backend) and keep only a locator reference in the document; where database residency is required, wrap the fields in application-level envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM keyed from KMS) and mask on serialisation; store user_password only as an irreversible hash (bcrypt or argon2) instead of a raw BinaryField; add a model test asserting no credential field round-trips unencrypted.

Source: maxwell-secure-code-reviewer agent analysis (execute-scr) at pinned commit 70b3633e171a1b8d389b27bb901c84c34a0e9bf6; no scanner SARIF log exists for this target (scanners could not run: no scanner executor configured).

evidence.description: no security-requirements reference in any clause

description:
sdlc/policy.json (policyVersion 1.0.0, effectiveFrom 2026-04-01) references no secure coding standard, no threat-modelling requirement and no SECURITY.md. Glob for SECURITY.md/security.txt/THREAT_MODEL.md over both checkouts (mongodb-mcp-server at aaa72a04, onfinance-db-model-master at 70b3633) returns no file, and git grep for security across README.md, MCP_SERVER_LIBRARY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md returns only usage-time recommendations (environment variables over CLI args, least-privilege Atlas roles). NIST SSDF PO.1.2 requires security requirements to be defined; SEBI CSCRF PR.IP.S2 requires an implemented system development life cycle and maps to nist-ssdf-800-218 PO.1.1 and iso-27001-2022 A.8.25.

Impact: Developers and the permitted AI harnesses build and change order-routing and client-data code with no agreed secure coding standard or threat model to design against; security expectations exist only as after-the-fact scanner findings, which is the common root cause behind the open SCH-API, SCH-PII and ASVS findings on the gateway.

Remediation: Adopt a secure coding standard and a threat-modelling requirement referenced from sdlc/policy.json (SSDF PO.1.2), add a SECURITY.md at the root of both repos, and record the SDLC control ownership against sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2.

description:
dependencyPolicy.sbomRequired is false (line 66) although sebi-cscrf-2024 GV.SC.S5 requires an SBOM for all core and critical software and the company is a SEBI mid-size RE. mcp-gateway is the only application backing the order-routing critical function (details.json criticalFunctions) and its qa and prod environments run docker.io/mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server images (applications/mcp-gateway/README.md; registry images built by CI), yet no SBOM exists: applications/mcp-gateway/images/ and applications/db-models/images/ do not exist and no *.cdx.json is anywhere in the workspace. The CI docker build attaches an sbom attestation to the pushed image (docker-publish.yml line 87) but nothing is retained on file and the policy sets no sbomFormat.

Impact: No component inventory exists for the image running the order-routing critical function, so a disclosure like Log4Shell or an upstream supply-chain compromise cannot be matched against what actually runs in prod; a direct CSCRF GV.SC.S5 breach for a mid-size RE.

Remediation: Set sbomRequired true with sbomFormat CycloneDX in sdlc/policy.json; export the image SBOM at build (the buildx sbom: true attestation already carries it) and file it as applications/mcp-gateway/images/<imageId>.cdx.json; capture the image records via refresh-apps.

Remediation: Add an audit and remediation section to sdlc/policy.json: a security audit after every major change, a findings register with owners and the Sec-4.4 3-month closure SLA, and follow-up validation; record executed audits and closure in the soc ledger.

title: No security owner, approver role or owning team named for security-sensitive code paths

title: Integration-test mongod published unauthenticated on all interfaces of developer laptops
description:
tests/integration/tools/mongodb/mongot-community-setup/docker-compose.yml publishes mongod as "0:27017" (line 12), which binds a random host port on 0.0.0.0 rather than 127.0.0.1; config/mongod.conf sets bindIp: 0.0.0.0 (line 7); and the compose command (lines 4-7) starts mongod without --auth or a keyFile, so the test replica set accepts unauthenticated connections even though init-mongo.sh creates a scoped mongotUser. Remediation: Bind the published port to loopback (127.0.0.1:27017:27017), start mongod with --auth plus a keyFile for the replica set, and keep bindIp scoped to the compose network.
